144: /****************************************************************************
145:  * Name: gt9xx_i2c_read
146:  *
147:  * Description:
148:  *   Read a Touch Panel Register over I2C.
149:  *
150:  * Input Parameters:
151:  *   dev    - Touch Panel Device
152:  *   reg    - I2C Register to be read
153:  *   buf    - Receive Buffer
154:  *   buflen - Number of bytes to be read
155:  *
156:  * Returned Value:
157:  *   Zero (OK) on success; a negated errno value is returned on any failure.
158:  *
159:  ****************************************************************************/
160: 
161: static int gt9xx_i2c_read(FAR struct gt9xx_dev_s *dev,
162:                           uint16_t reg,
163:                           uint8_t *buf,
164:                           size_t buflen)
165: {
166:   int ret;
167: 
168:   /* Send the Register Address, MSB first */
169: 
170:   uint8_t regbuf[2] =
171:   {
172:     reg >> 8,   /* First Byte: MSB */
173:     reg & 0xff  /* Second Byte: LSB */
174:   };
175: 
176:   /* Compose the I2C Messages */
177: 
178:   struct i2c_msg_s msgv[2] =
179:   {
180:     {
181:       /* Send the I2C Register Address */
182: 
183:       .frequency = CONFIG_INPUT_GT9XX_I2C_FREQUENCY,
184:       .addr      = dev->addr,
185:       .flags     = 0,
186:       .buffer    = regbuf,
187:       .length    = sizeof(regbuf)
188:     },
189:     {
190:       /* Receive the I2C Register Values */
191: 
192:       .frequency = CONFIG_INPUT_GT9XX_I2C_FREQUENCY,
193:       .addr      = dev->addr,
194:       .flags     = I2C_M_READ,
195:       .buffer    = buf,
196:       .length    = buflen
197:     }
198:   };
199: 
200:   const int msgv_len = sizeof(msgv) / sizeof(msgv[0]);
201: 
202:   iinfo("reg=0x%x, buflen=%ld\n", reg, buflen);
203:   DEBUGASSERT(dev && dev->i2c && buf);
204: 
205:   /* Execute the I2C Transfer */
206: 
207:   ret = I2C_TRANSFER(dev->i2c, msgv, msgv_len);
208:   if (ret < 0)
209:     {
210:       ierr("I2C Read failed: %d\n", ret);
211:       return ret;
212:     }
213: 
214: #ifdef CONFIG_DEBUG_INPUT_INFO
215:   iinfodumpbuffer("gt9xx_i2c_read", buf, buflen);
216: #endif /* CONFIG_DEBUG_INPUT_INFO */
217: 
218:   return OK;
219: }

221: /****************************************************************************
222:  * Name: gt9xx_i2c_write
223:  *
224:  * Description:
225:  *   Write to a Touch Panel Register over I2C.
226:  *
227:  * Input Parameters:
228:  *   dev - Touch Panel Device
229:  *   reg - I2C Register to be written
230:  *   val - Value to be written
231:  *
232:  * Returned Value:
233:  *   Zero (OK) on success; a negated errno value is returned on any failure.
234:  *
235:  ****************************************************************************/
236: 
237: static int gt9xx_i2c_write(FAR struct gt9xx_dev_s *dev,
238:                            uint16_t reg,
239:                            uint8_t val)
240: {
241:   int ret;
242: 
243:   /* Send the Register Address, MSB first */
244: 
245:   uint8_t regbuf[2] =
246:   {
247:     reg >> 8,   /* First Byte: MSB */
248:     reg & 0xff  /* Second Byte: LSB */
249:   };
250: 
251:   /* Send the Register Value */
252: 
253:   uint8_t buf[1] =
254:   {
255:     val  /* Value to be written */
256:   };
257: 
258:   /* Compose the I2C Messages */
259: 
260:   struct i2c_msg_s msgv[2] =
261:   {
262:     {
263:       /* Send the I2C Register Address */
264: 
265:       .frequency = CONFIG_INPUT_GT9XX_I2C_FREQUENCY,
266:       .addr      = dev->addr,
267:       .flags     = 0,
268:       .buffer    = regbuf,
269:       .length    = sizeof(regbuf)
270:     },
271:     {
272:       /* Send the I2C Register Value */
273: 
274:       .frequency = CONFIG_INPUT_GT9XX_I2C_FREQUENCY,
275:       .addr      = dev->addr,
276:       .flags     = I2C_M_NOSTART,
277:       .buffer    = buf,
278:       .length    = sizeof(buf)
279:     }
280:   };
281: 
282:   const int msgv_len = sizeof(msgv) / sizeof(msgv[0]);
283: 
284:   iinfo("reg=0x%x, val=%d\n", reg, val);
285:   DEBUGASSERT(dev && dev->i2c);
286: 
287:   /* Execute the I2C Transfer */
288: 
289:   ret = I2C_TRANSFER(dev->i2c, msgv, msgv_len);
290:   if (ret < 0)
291:     {
292:       ierr("I2C Write failed: %d\n", ret);
293:       return ret;
294:     }
295: 
296:   return OK;
297: }

370: /****************************************************************************
371:  * Name: gt9xx_read_touch_data
372:  *
373:  * Description:
374:  *   Read a Touch Sample from Touch Panel. Returns either 0 or 1
375:  *   Touch Points.
376:  *
377:  * Input Parameters:
378:  *   dev    - Touch Panel Device
379:  *   sample - Returned Touch Sample (0 or 1 Touch Points)
380:  *
381:  * Returned Value:
382:  *   Zero (OK) on success; a negated errno value is returned on any failure.
383:  *
384:  ****************************************************************************/
385: 
386: static int gt9xx_read_touch_data(FAR struct gt9xx_dev_s *dev,
387:                                  FAR struct touch_sample_s *sample)
388: {
389:   uint8_t status[1];
390:   uint8_t status_code;
391:   uint8_t touched_points;
392:   uint8_t touch[6];
393:   uint16_t x;
394:   uint16_t y;
395:   uint8_t flags;
396:   int ret;
397: 
398:   /* Erase the Touch Sample and Touch Point */
399: 
400:   iinfo("\n");
401:   DEBUGASSERT(dev && sample);
402:   memset(sample, 0, sizeof(*sample));
403: 
404:   /* Read the Touch Panel Status */
405: 
406:   ret = gt9xx_i2c_read(dev, GTP_READ_COOR_ADDR, status, sizeof(status));
407:   if (ret < 0)
408:     {
409:       ierr("Read Touch Panel Status failed: %d\n", ret);
410:       return ret;
411:     }
412: 
413:   /* Decode the Status Code and the Touched Points */
414: 
415:   status_code = status[0] & 0x80;
416:   touched_points = status[0] & 0x0f;
417: 
418:   /* If Touch Panel Status is OK and Touched Points is 1 or more */
419: 
420:   if (status_code != 0 && touched_points >= 1)
421:     {
422:       /* Read the First Touch Point (6 bytes) */
423: 
424:       ret = gt9xx_i2c_read(dev, GTP_POINT1, touch, sizeof(touch));
425:       if (ret < 0)
426:         {
427:           ierr("Read Touch Point failed: %d\n", ret);
428:           return ret;
429:         }
430: 
431:       /* Decode the Touch Coordinates */
432: 
433:       x = touch[0] + (touch[1] << 8);
434:       y = touch[2] + (touch[3] << 8);
435: 
436:       /* Return the Touch Coordinates as Touch Down */
437: 
438:       flags = TOUCH_DOWN | TOUCH_ID_VALID | TOUCH_POS_VALID;
439:       sample->npoints = 1;
440:       sample->point[0].id = 0;
441:       sample->point[0].x = x;
442:       sample->point[0].y = y;
443:       sample->point[0].flags = flags;
444:       iinfo("touch down x=%d, y=%d\n", x, y);
445:     }
446: 
447:   /* Set the Touch Panel Status to 0 */
448: 
449:   ret = gt9xx_set_status(dev, 0);
450:   if (ret < 0)
451:     {
452:       ierr("Set Touch Panel Status failed: %d\n", ret);
453:       return ret;
454:     }
455: 
456:   return OK;
457: }

459: /****************************************************************************
460:  * Name: gt9xx_read
461:  *
462:  * Description:
463:  *   Read a Touch Sample from Touch Panel. Returns either 0 or 1
464:  *   Touch Points.
465:  *
466:  * Input Parameters:
467:  *   dev    - Touch Panel Device
468:  *   buffer - Returned Touch Sample (0 or 1 Touch Points)
469:  *   buflen - Size of buffer
470:  *
471:  * Returned Value:
472:  *   Zero (OK) on success; a negated errno value is returned on any failure.
473:  *
474:  ****************************************************************************/
475: 
476: static ssize_t gt9xx_read(FAR struct file *filep, FAR char *buffer,
477:                           size_t buflen)
478: {
479:   FAR struct inode *inode;
480:   FAR struct gt9xx_dev_s *priv;
481:   struct touch_sample_s sample;
482:   const size_t outlen = sizeof(sample);
483:   irqstate_t flags;
484:   int ret;
485: 
486:   /* Returned Touch Sample will have 0 or 1 Touch Points */
487: 
488:   iinfo("buflen=%ld\n", buflen);
489:   if (buflen < outlen)
490:     {
491:       ierr("Buffer should be at least %ld bytes, got %ld bytes\n",
492:            outlen, buflen);
493:       return -EINVAL;
494:     }
495: 
496:   /* Get the Touch Panel Device */
497: 
498:   inode = filep->f_inode;
499:   DEBUGASSERT(inode->i_private);
500:   priv = inode->i_private;
501: 
502:   /* Begin Mutex: Lock to prevent concurrent reads */
503: 
504:   ret = nxmutex_lock(&priv->devlock);
505:   if (ret < 0)
506:     {
507:       return ret;
508:     }
509: 
510:   ret = -EINVAL;
511: 
512:   /* If waiting for Touch Up, return the Last Touch Point as Touch Up */
513: 
514:   if (priv->flags & TOUCH_DOWN)
515:     {
516:       /* Begin Critical Section */
517: 
518:       flags = enter_critical_section();
519: 
520:       /* Mark the Last Touch Point as Touch Up */
521: 
522:       priv->flags = TOUCH_UP | TOUCH_ID_VALID | TOUCH_POS_VALID;
523: 
524:       /* End Critical Section */
525: 
526:       leave_critical_section(flags);
527: 
528:       /* Return the Last Touch Point, changed to Touch Up */
529: 
530:       memset(&sample, 0, sizeof(sample));
531:       sample.npoints = 1;
532:       sample.point[0].id = 0;
533:       sample.point[0].x = priv->x;
534:       sample.point[0].y = priv->y;
535:       sample.point[0].flags = priv->flags;
536:       memcpy(buffer, &sample, sizeof(sample));
537:       ret = OK;
538:       iinfo("touch up x=%d, y=%d\n", priv->x, priv->y);
539:     }
540:   else
541:     {
542:       /* Otherwise read the Touch Point over I2C */
543: 
544:       ret = gt9xx_read_touch_data(priv, &sample);
545: 
546:       /* Skip duplicates */
547: 
548:       if (sample.npoints >= 1 &&
549:           priv->x == sample.point[0].x &&
550:           priv->y == sample.point[0].y)
551:         {
552:           memset(&sample, 0, sizeof(sample));
553:           sample.npoints = 0;
554:           iinfo("skip duplicate x=%d, y=%d\n", priv->x, priv->y);
555:         }
556: 
557:       /* Return the Touch Point */
558: 
559:       memcpy(buffer, &sample, sizeof(sample));
560: 
561:       /* Begin Critical Section */
562: 
563:       flags = enter_critical_section();
564: 
565:       /* Clear the Interrupt Pending Flag */
566: 
567:       priv->int_pending = false;
568: 
569:       /* Remember the Last Touch Point */
570: 
571:       if (sample.npoints >= 1)
572:         {
573:           priv->x = sample.point[0].x;
574:           priv->y = sample.point[0].y;
575:           priv->flags = sample.point[0].flags;
576:         }
577: 
578:       /* End Critical Section */
579: 
580:       leave_critical_section(flags);
581:     }
582: 
583:   /* End Mutex: Unlock to allow next read */
584: 
585:   nxmutex_unlock(&priv->devlock);
586:   return (ret < 0) ? ret : outlen;
587: }

589: /****************************************************************************
590:  * Name: gt9xx_open
591:  *
592:  * Description:
593:  *   Open the Touch Panel Device.  If this is the first open, we power on
594:  *   the Touch Panel, probe for the Touch Panel and enable Touch Panel
595:  *   Interrupts.
596:  *
597:  * Input Parameters:
598:  *   filep - File Struct for Touch Panel
599:  *
600:  * Returned Value:
601:  *   Zero (OK) on success; a negated errno value is returned on any failure.
602:  *
603:  ****************************************************************************/
604: 
605: static int gt9xx_open(FAR struct file *filep)
606: {
607:   FAR struct inode *inode;
608:   FAR struct gt9xx_dev_s *priv;
609:   unsigned int use_count;
610:   int ret;
611: 
612:   /* Get the Touch Panel Device */
613: 
614:   iinfo("\n");
615:   inode = filep->f_inode;
616:   DEBUGASSERT(inode->i_private);
617:   priv = inode->i_private;
618: 
619:   /* Begin Mutex: Lock to prevent concurrent update to Reference Count */
620: 
621:   ret = nxmutex_lock(&priv->devlock);
622:   if (ret < 0)
623:     {
624:       ierr("Lock Mutex failed: %d\n", ret);
625:       return ret;
626:     }
627: 
628:   /* Get next Reference Count */
629: 
630:   use_count = priv->cref + 1;
631:   DEBUGASSERT(use_count < UINT8_MAX && use_count > priv->cref);
632:   if (use_count == 1)
633:     {
634:       /* If first user, power on the Touch Panel */
635: 
636:       DEBUGASSERT(priv->board->set_power != NULL);
637:       ret = priv->board->set_power(priv->board, true);
638:       if (ret < 0)
639:         {
640:           goto out_lock;
641:         }
642: 
643:       /* Let Touch Panel power up before probing */
644: 
645:       nxsig_usleep(100 * 1000);
646: 
647:       /* Check that Touch Panel exists on I2C */
648: 
649:       ret = gt9xx_probe_device(priv);
650:       if (ret < 0)
651:         {
652:           /* No such device, power off the Touch Panel */
653: 
654:           priv->board->set_power(priv->board, false);
655:           goto out_lock;
656:         }
657: 
658:       /* Enable Touch Panel Interrupts */
659: 
660:       DEBUGASSERT(priv->board->irq_enable);
661:       priv->board->irq_enable(priv->board, true);
662:     }
663: 
664:   /* Set the Reference Count */
665: 
666:   priv->cref = use_count;
667: 
668:   /* End Mutex: Unlock to allow update to Reference Count */
669: 
670: out_lock:
671:   nxmutex_unlock(&priv->devlock);
672:   return ret;
673: }

675: /****************************************************************************
676:  * Name: gt9xx_close
677:  *
678:  * Description:
679:  *   Close the Touch Panel Device.  If this is the final close, we disable
680:  *   Touch Panel Interrupts and power off the Touch Panel.
681:  *
682:  * Input Parameters:
683:  *   filep - File Struct for Touch Panel
684:  *
685:  * Returned Value:
686:  *   Zero (OK) on success; a negated errno value is returned on any failure.
687:  *
688:  ****************************************************************************/
689: 
690: static int gt9xx_close(FAR struct file *filep)
691: {
692:   FAR struct inode *inode;
693:   FAR struct gt9xx_dev_s *priv;
694:   int use_count;
695:   int ret;
696: 
697:   /* Get the Touch Panel Device */
698: 
699:   iinfo("\n");
700:   inode = filep->f_inode;
701:   DEBUGASSERT(inode->i_private);
702:   priv = inode->i_private;
703: 
704:   /* Begin Mutex: Lock to prevent concurrent update to Reference Count */
705: 
706:   ret = nxmutex_lock(&priv->devlock);
707:   if (ret < 0)
708:     {
709:       ierr("Lock Mutex failed: %d\n", ret);
710:       return ret;
711:     }
712: 
713:   /* Decrement the Reference Count */
714: 
715:   use_count = priv->cref - 1;
716:   DEBUGASSERT(use_count >= 0);
717:   if (use_count == 0)
718:     {
719:       /* If final user, disable Touch Panel Interrupts */
720: 
721:       DEBUGASSERT(priv->board && priv->board->irq_enable);
722:       priv->board->irq_enable(priv->board, false);
723: 
724:       /* Power off the Touch Panel */
725: 
726:       DEBUGASSERT(priv->board->set_power);
727:       priv->board->set_power(priv->board, false);
728:     }
729: 
730:   /* Set the Reference Count */
731: 
732:   priv->cref = use_count;
733: 
734:   /* End Mutex: Unlock to allow update to Reference Count */
735: 
736:   nxmutex_unlock(&priv->devlock);
737:   return OK;
738: }

740: /****************************************************************************
741:  * Name: gt9xx_ioctl
742:  *
743:  * Description:
744:  *   Handle Touch Panel specific commands.
745:  *
746:  * Input Parameters:
747:  *   filep - File Struct for Touch Panel
748:  *   cmd   - The ioctl command
749:  *   arg   - The ioctl argument
750:  *
751:  * Returned Value:
752:  *   Zero (OK) on success; a negated errno value is returned on any failure.
753:  *

756: static int gt9xx_ioctl(FAR struct file *filep, int cmd, unsigned long arg)
757: {
758:   UNUSED(filep);
759: 
760:   switch (cmd)
761:     {
762:       case TSIOC_GETMAXPOINTS:
763:         {
764:           FAR uint8_t *maxpoints = (FAR uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)arg;
765: 
766:           if (maxpoints == NULL)
767:             {
768:               return -EINVAL;
769:             }
770:

773:         }

777:     }

780: /****************************************************************************
781:  * Name: gt9xx_poll
782:  *
783:  * Description:
784:  *   Setup or teardown a poll for the Touch Panel Device.
785:  *
786:  * Input Parameters:
787:  *   filep - File Struct for Touch Panel
788:  *   fds   - The structure describing the events to be monitored, OR NULL if
789:  *           this is a request to stop monitoring events.
790:  *   setup - true: Setup the poll; false: Teardown the poll
791:  *
792:  * Returned Value:
793:  *   Zero (OK) on success; a negated errno value is returned on any failure.
794:  *
795:  ****************************************************************************/
796: 
797: static int gt9xx_poll(FAR struct file *filep, FAR struct pollfd *fds,
798:                       bool setup)
799: {
800:   FAR struct gt9xx_dev_s *priv;
801:   FAR struct inode *inode;
802:   bool pending;
803:   int ret = 0;
804:   int i;
805: 
806:   /* Get the Touch Panel Device */
807: 
808:   iinfo("setup=%d\n", setup);
809:   DEBUGASSERT(fds);
810:   inode = filep->f_inode;
811:   DEBUGASSERT(inode->i_private);
812:   priv = inode->i_private;
813: 
814:   /* Begin Mutex: Lock to prevent concurrent update to Poll Waiters */
815: 
816:   ret = nxmutex_lock(&priv->devlock);
817:   if (ret < 0)
818:     {
819:       ierr("Lock Mutex failed: %d\n", ret);
820:       return ret;
821:     }
822: 
823:   if (setup)
824:     {
825:       /* If Poll Setup: Ignore waits that do not include POLLIN */
826: 
827:       if ((fds->events & POLLIN) == 0)
828:         {
829:           ret = -EDEADLK;
830:           goto out;
831:         }
832: 
833:       /* Find an available slot for the Poll Waiter */
834: 
835:       for (i = 0; i < CONFIG_INPUT_GT9XX_NPOLLWAITERS; i++)
836:         {
837:           /* Found an available slot */
838: 
839:           if (!priv->fds[i])
840:             {
841:               /* Bind the poll structure and this slot */
842: 
843:               priv->fds[i] = fds;
844:               fds->priv = &priv->fds[i];
845:               break;
846:             }
847:         }
848: 
849:       if (i >= CONFIG_INPUT_GT9XX_NPOLLWAITERS)
850:         {
851:           /* No slots available */
852: 
853:           fds->priv = NULL;
854:           ret = -EBUSY;
855:         }
856:       else
857:         {
858:           /* If Interrupt Pending is set, notify the Poll Waiters */
859: 
860:           pending = priv->int_pending;
861:           if (pending)
862:             {
863:               poll_notify(&fds, 1, POLLIN);
864:             }
865:         }
866:     }
867:   else if (fds->priv)
868:     {
869:       /* If Poll Teardown: Remove the poll setup */
870: 
871:       FAR struct pollfd **slot = (FAR struct pollfd **)fds->priv;
872:       DEBUGASSERT(slot != NULL);
873: 
874:       *slot = NULL;
875:       fds->priv = NULL;
876:     }
877: 
878:   /* End Mutex: Unlock to allow update to Poll Waiters */
879: 
880: out:
881:   nxmutex_unlock(&priv->devlock);
882:   return ret;
883: }
884: 
885: /****************************************************************************
886:  * Name: gt9xx_isr_handler
887:  *
888:  * Description:
889:  *   Interrupt Handler for Touch Panel.
890:  *
891:  * Input Parameters:
892:  *   irq     - IRQ Number
893:  *   context - IRQ Context
894:  *   arg     - Touch Panel Device
895:  *
896:  * Returned Value:
897:  *   Zero (OK) on success; a negated errno value is returned on any failure.
898:  *
899:  ****************************************************************************/
900: 
901: static int gt9xx_isr_handler(int irq, FAR void *context, FAR void *arg)
902: {
903:   FAR struct gt9xx_dev_s *priv = (FAR struct gt9xx_dev_s *)arg;
904:   irqstate_t flags;
905: 
906:   DEBUGASSERT(priv);
907: 
908:   /* Begin Critical Section */
909: 
910:   flags = enter_critical_section();
911: 
912:   /* Set the Interrupt Pending Flag */
913: 
914:   priv->int_pending = true;
915: 
916:   /* End Critical Section */
917: 
918:   leave_critical_section(flags);
919: 
920:   /* Notify the Poll Waiters */
921: 
922:   poll_notify(priv->fds, CONFIG_INPUT_GT9XX_NPOLLWAITERS, POLLIN);
923:   return OK;
924: }
925: 
926: /****************************************************************************
927:  * Public Functions
928:  ****************************************************************************/
929: 
930: /****************************************************************************
931:  * Name: gt9xx_register
932:  *
933:  * Description:
934:  *   Register the driver for Goodix GT9XX Touch Panel.  Attach the
935:  *   Interrupt Handler for the Touch Panel and disable Touch Interrupts.
936:  *
937:  * Input Parameters:
938:  *   devpath      - Device Path (e.g. "/dev/input0")
939:  *   dev          - I2C Bus
940:  *   i2c_devaddr  - I2C Address of Touch Panel
941:  *   board_config - Callback for Board-Specific Operations
942:  *
943:  * Returned Value:
944:  *   Zero (OK) on success; a negated errno value is returned on any failure.
945:  *
946:  ****************************************************************************/
947: 
948: int gt9xx_register(FAR const char *devpath,
949:                    FAR struct i2c_master_s *i2c_dev,
950:                    uint8_t i2c_devaddr,
951:                    const struct gt9xx_board_s *board_config)
952: {
953:   struct gt9xx_dev_s *priv;
954:   int ret = 0;
955: 
956:   iinfo("devpath=%s, i2c_devaddr=%d\n", devpath, i2c_devaddr);
957:   DEBUGASSERT(devpath != NULL && i2c_dev != NULL && board_config != NULL);
958: 
959:   /* Allocate the Touch Panel Device Structure */
960: 
961:   priv = kmm_zalloc(sizeof(struct gt9xx_dev_s));
962:   if (!priv)
963:     {
964:       ierr("GT9XX Memory Allocation failed\n");
965:       return -ENOMEM;
966:     }
967: 
968:   /* Setup the Touch Panel Device Structure */
969: 
970:   priv->addr = i2c_devaddr;
971:   priv->i2c = i2c_dev;
972:   priv->board = board_config;
973:   nxmutex_init(&priv->devlock);
974: 
975:   /* Register the Touch Input Driver */
976: 
977:   ret = register_driver(devpath, &g_gt9xx_fileops, 0666, priv);
978:   if (ret < 0)
979:     {
980:       nxmutex_destroy(&priv->devlock);
981:       kmm_free(priv);
982:       ierr("GT9XX Registration failed: %d\n", ret);
983:       return ret;
984:     }
985: 
986:   /* Attach the Interrupt Handler */
987: 
988:   DEBUGASSERT(priv->board->irq_attach);
989:   priv->board->irq_attach(priv->board, gt9xx_isr_handler, priv);
990: 
991:   /* Disable Touch Panel Interrupts */
992: 
993:   DEBUGASSERT(priv->board->irq_enable);
994:   priv->board->irq_enable(priv->board, false);
995: 
996:   iinfo("GT9XX Touch Panel registered\n");
997:   return OK;
998: }

84:  * activity.  These definitions represent the maximum and the minimum
85:  * polling rates.

96: /* This structure describes the state of one FT5x06 driver instance */
97: 
98: struct ft5x06_dev_s
99: {
100:   uint8_t crefs;                            /* Number of times the device
101:                                              * has been opened */
102:   uint8_t nwaiters;                         /* Number of threads waiting for
103:                                              * FT5x06 data */
104:   volatile bool valid;                      /* True:  New, valid touch data
105:                                              * in touchbuf[] */
106: #ifdef CONFIG_FT5X06_SINGLEPOINT
107:   uint8_t lastid;                           /* Last reported touch id */
108:   uint8_t lastevent;                        /* Last reported event */
109:   int16_t lastx;                            /* Last reported X position */
110:   int16_t lasty;                            /* Last reported Y position */
111: #endif
112:   mutex_t devlock;                          /* Manages exclusive access to
113:                                              * this structure */
114:   sem_t waitsem;                            /* Used to wait for the
115:                                              * availability of data */
116:   uint32_t frequency;                       /* Current I2C frequency */
117: #ifdef CONFIG_FT5X06_POLLMODE
118:   uint32_t delay;                           /* Current poll delay */
119: #endif
120: 
121:   FAR const struct ft5x06_config_s *config; /* Board configuration data */
122:   FAR struct i2c_master_s *i2c;             /* Saved I2C driver instance */
123:   struct work_s work;                       /* Supports the interrupt
124:                                              * handling "bottom half" */
125: #ifdef CONFIG_FT5X06_POLLMODE
126:   struct wdog_s polltimer;                  /* Poll timer */
127: #endif
128:   uint8_t touchbuf[FT5X06_TOUCH_DATA_LEN];  /* Raw touch data */
129: 
130:   /* The following is a list if poll structures of threads waiting for
131:    * driver events. The 'struct pollfd' reference for each open is also
132:    * retained in the f_priv field of the 'struct file'.
133:    */
134: 
135:   FAR struct pollfd *fds[CONFIG_FT5X06_NPOLLWAITERS];
136: };

200: /****************************************************************************
201:  * Name: ft5x06_notify
202:  ****************************************************************************/
203: 
204: static void ft5x06_notify(FAR struct ft5x06_dev_s *priv)
205: {
206:   /* If there are threads waiting on poll() for FT5x06 data to become
207:    * available, then wake them up now.  NOTE: we wake up all waiting threads
208:    * because we do not know that they are going to do.  If they all try to
209:    * read the data, then some make end up blocking after all.
210:    */
211: 
212:   poll_notify(priv->fds, CONFIG_FT5X06_NPOLLWAITERS, POLLIN);
213: 
214:   /* If there are threads waiting for read data, then signal one of them
215:    * that the read data is available.
216:    */
217: 
218:   if (priv->nwaiters > 0)
219:     {
220:       /* After posting this semaphore, we need to exit because the FT5x06
221:        * is no longer available.
222:        */
223: 
224:       nxsem_post(&priv->waitsem);
225:     }
226: }
227: 
228: /****************************************************************************
229:  * Name: ft5x06_data_worker
230:  ****************************************************************************/
231: 
232: static void ft5x06_data_worker(FAR void *arg)
233: {
234:   FAR struct ft5x06_dev_s *priv = (FAR struct ft5x06_dev_s *)arg;
235:   FAR const struct ft5x06_config_s *config;
236:   FAR struct ft5x06_touch_data_s *sample;
237:   struct i2c_msg_s msg[2];
238:   uint8_t regaddr;
239:   int ret;
240: 
241:   /* Get a pointer the callbacks for convenience */
242: 
243:   DEBUGASSERT(priv != NULL && priv->config != NULL);
244:   config = priv->config;
245: 
246:   /* We need to have exclusive access to the touchbuf so that we do not
247:    * corrupt any read operation that is in place.
248:    */
249: 
250:   nxmutex_lock(&priv->devlock);
251: 
252:   /* Read touch data */
253: 
254:   /* Set up the address write operation */
255: 
256:   regaddr          = FT5X06_TOUCH_DATA_STARTREG;
257: 
258:   msg[0].frequency = priv->frequency;       /* I2C frequency */
259:   msg[0].addr      = config->address;       /* 7-bit address */
260:   msg[0].flags     = 0;                     /* Write transaction with START */
261:   msg[0].buffer    = ®addr;              /* Send one byte of data (no STOP) */
262:   msg[0].length    = 1;
263: 
264:   /* Set up the data read operation.
265:    *
266:    * REVISIT:  If CONFIG_FT5X06_SINGLEPOINT is selected, could we not just
267:    * set the length for one sample?  Or is there some reason why we have to
268:    * read all of the points?
269:    */
270: 
271:   msg[1].frequency = priv->frequency;       /* I2C frequency */
272:   msg[1].addr      = config->address;       /* 7-bit address */
273:   msg[1].flags     = I2C_M_READ;            /* Read transaction with Re-START */
274:   msg[1].buffer    = priv->touchbuf;        /* Read all touch data */
275:   msg[1].length    = FT5X06_TOUCH_DATA_LEN;
276: 
277:   ret = I2C_TRANSFER(priv->i2c, msg, 2);
278:   if (ret >= 0)
279:     {
280:       /* In polled mode, we may read invalid touch data.  If there is
281:        * no touch data, the FT5x06 returns all 0xff the very first time.
282:        * After that, it returns the same old stale data when there is
283:        * no touch data.
284:        */
285: 
286:       sample = (FAR struct ft5x06_touch_data_s *)priv->touchbuf;
287: 
288:       /* Notify waiters (only if we ready some valid data).
289:        *
290:        * REVISIT: For improved performance consider moving the duplicate
291:        * report and thresholding logic from ft5x06_sample() to here.  That
292:        * would save a context switch.
293:        */
294: 
295:       if (sample->tdstatus <= FT5X06_MAX_TOUCHES)
296:         {
297:           /* Notify any waiters that new FT5x06 data is available */
298: 
299:           priv->valid = true;
300:           ft5x06_notify(priv);
301:         }
302: 
303: #ifdef CONFIG_FT5X06_POLLMODE
304:       /* Update the poll rate */
305: 
306:       if (sample->tdstatus > 0 && sample->tdstatus <= FT5X06_MAX_TOUCHES)
307:         {
308:           /* Keep it at the minimum if touches are detected. */
309: 
310:           priv->delay = POLL_MINDELAY;
311:         }
312:       else if (priv->delay < POLL_MAXDELAY)
313:         {
314:           /* Otherwise, let the poll rate rise gradually up to the maximum
315:            * if there is no touch.
316:            */
317: 
318:           priv->delay += POLL_INCREMENT;
319:         }
320: #endif
321:     }
322: 
323: #ifdef CONFIG_FT5X06_POLLMODE
324:   /* Exit, re-starting the poll. */
325: 
326:   wd_start(&priv->polltimer, priv->delay,
327:            ft5x06_poll_timeout, (wdparm_t)priv);
328: 
329: #else
330:   /* Exit, re-enabling FT5x06 interrupts */
331: 
332:   config->enable(config, true);
333: #endif
334: 
335:   nxmutex_unlock(&priv->devlock);
336: }

338: /****************************************************************************
339:  * Name: ft5x06_poll_timeout
340:  ****************************************************************************/
341: 
342: #ifdef CONFIG_FT5X06_POLLMODE
343: static void ft5x06_poll_timeout(wdparm_t arg)
344: {
345:   FAR struct ft5x06_dev_s *priv = (FAR struct ft5x06_dev_s *)arg;
346:   int ret;
347: 
348:   /* Transfer processing to the worker thread.  Since FT5x06 poll timer is
349:    * disabled while the work is pending, no special action should be
350:    * required to protected the work queue.
351:    */
352: 
353:   DEBUGASSERT(priv->work.worker == NULL);
354:   ret = work_queue(HPWORK, &priv->work, ft5x06_data_worker, priv, 0);
355:   if (ret != 0)
356:     {
357:       ierr("ERROR: Failed to queue work: %d\n", ret);
358:     }

363:  * Name: ft5x06_data_interrupt
364:  ****************************************************************************/
365: 
366: #ifndef CONFIG_FT5X06_POLLMODE
367: static int ft5x06_data_interrupt(int irq, FAR void *context, FAR void *arg)
368: {
369:   FAR struct ft5x06_dev_s *priv = (FAR struct ft5x06_dev_s *)arg;
370:   FAR const struct ft5x06_config_s *config;
371:   int ret;
372: 
373:   /* Get a pointer the callbacks for convenience (and so the code is not so
374:    * ugly).
375:    */
376: 
377:   config = priv->config;
378:   DEBUGASSERT(config != NULL);
379: 
380:   /* Disable further interrupts */
381: 
382:   config->enable(config, false);
383: 
384:   /* Transfer processing to the worker thread.  Since FT5x06 interrupts are
385:    * disabled while the work is pending, no special action should be required
386:    * to protected the work queue.
387:    */
388: 
389:   DEBUGASSERT(priv->work.worker == NULL);
390:   ret = work_queue(HPWORK, &priv->work, ft5x06_data_worker, priv, 0);
391:   if (ret != 0)
392:     {
393:       ierr("ERROR: Failed to queue work: %d\n", ret);
394:     }
395: 
396:   /* Clear any pending interrupts and return success */
397: 
398:   config->clear(config);
399:   return OK;
400: }

403: /****************************************************************************
404:  * Name: ft5x06_sample
405:  ****************************************************************************/
406: 
407: #ifdef CONFIG_FT5X06_SINGLEPOINT
408: static ssize_t ft5x06_sample(FAR struct ft5x06_dev_s *priv, FAR char *buffer,
409:                              size_t len)
410: {
411:   FAR struct ft5x06_touch_data_s *raw;
412:   FAR struct ft5x06_touch_point_s *touch;
413:   FAR struct touch_sample_s *sample;
414:   FAR struct touch_point_s *point;
415:   int16_t x;
416:   int16_t y;
417:   uint8_t event;
418:   uint8_t id;
419: 
420:   if (!priv->valid)
421:     {
422:       return 0;  /* Nothing to read */
423:     }
424: 
425:   /* Raw data pointers (source) */
426: 
427:   raw = (FAR struct ft5x06_touch_data_s *)priv->touchbuf;
428:   touch = raw->touch;
429: 
430:   /* Get the reported X and Y positions */
431: 
432:   #ifdef CONFIG_FT5X06_SWAPXY
433:   y = TOUCH_POINT_GET_X(touch[0]);
434:   x = TOUCH_POINT_GET_Y(touch[0]);
435: #else
436:   x = TOUCH_POINT_GET_X(touch[0]);
437:   y = TOUCH_POINT_GET_Y(touch[0]);
438: #endif
439: 
440:   /* Get the touch point ID and event */
441: 
442:   event = TOUCH_POINT_GET_EVENT(touch[0]);
443:   id    = TOUCH_POINT_GET_ID(touch[0]);
444: 
445:   if (event == FT5X06_INVALID)
446:     {
447:       priv->lastevent = FT5X06_INVALID;
448:       goto reset_and_drop;
449:     }
450: 
451:   if (id == priv->lastid && event == priv->lastevent)
452:     {
453:       /* Same ID and event..  Is there positional data? */
454: 
455:       if (raw->tdstatus == 0 || event == FT5X06_UP)
456:         {
457:           /* No... no new touch data */
458: 
459:           goto reset_and_drop;
460:         }
461:       else
462:         {
463:           int16_t deltax;
464:           int16_t deltay;
465: 
466:           /* Compare the change in position from the last report. */
467: 
468:           deltax = (x - priv->lastx);
469:           if (deltax < 0)
470:             {
471:               deltax = -deltax;
472:             }
473: 
474:           if (deltax < CONFIG_FT5X06_THRESHX)
475:             {
476:               /* There as been no significant change in X, try Y */
477: 
478:               deltay = (y - priv->lasty);
479:               if (deltay < 0)
480:                 {
481:                   deltay = -deltay;
482:                 }
483: 
484:               if (deltax < CONFIG_FT5X06_THRESHX)
485:                 {
486:                   /* Ignore... no significant change in Y either */
487: 
488:                   goto drop;
489:                 }
490:             }
491:         }
492:     }
493: 
494:   priv->lastid      = id;
495:   priv->lastevent   = event;
496:   priv->lastx       = x;
497:   priv->lasty       = y;
498: 
499:   /* User data buffer points (sink) */
500: 
501:   /* Return the number of touches read */
502: 
503:   sample            = (FAR struct touch_sample_s *)buffer;
504:   sample->npoints   = 1;
505: 
506:   /* Decode and return the single touch point */
507: 
508:   point             = sample->point;
509:   point[0].id       = id;
510:   point[0].flags    = g_event_map[event];
511:   point[0].x        = x;
512:   point[0].y        = y;
513:   point[0].h        = 0;
514:   point[0].w        = 0;
515:   point[0].pressure = 0;
516: 
517:   priv->valid       = false;
518:   return SIZEOF_TOUCH_SAMPLE_S(1);
519: 
520: reset_and_drop:
521:   priv->lastx = 0;
522:   priv->lasty = 0;
523: drop:
524:   priv->valid = false;
525:   return 0;  /* No new touches read. */
526: }
527: #else
528: static ssize_t ft5x06_sample(FAR struct ft5x06_dev_s *priv, FAR char *buffer,
529:                              size_t len)
530: {
531:   FAR struct ft5x06_touch_data_s *raw;
532:   FAR struct ft5x06_touch_point_s *touch;
533:   FAR struct touch_sample_s *sample;
534:   FAR struct touch_point_s *point;
535:   unsigned int maxtouches;
536:   unsigned int ntouches;
537:   int i;
538: 
539:   maxtouches = (len - sizeof(int)) / sizeof(struct touch_point_s);
540:   DEBUGASSERT(maxtouches > 0);  /* Already verified */
541: 
542:   if (!priv->valid)
543:     {
544:       return 0;  /* Nothing to read */
545:     }
546: 
547:   /* Raw data pointers (source) */
548: 
549:   raw      = (FAR struct ft5x06_touch_data_s *)priv->touchbuf;
550:   touch    = raw->touch;
551: 
552:   /* Decode number of touches */
553: 
554:   ntouches = raw->tdstatus;
555:   DEBUGASSERT(ntouches <= FT5X06_MAX_TOUCHES);
556: 
557:   if (ntouches > maxtouches)
558:     {
559:       ntouches = maxtouches;
560:     }
561: 
562:   if (ntouches < 1)
563:     {
564:       priv->valid = false;
565:       return 0;  /* No touches read. */
566:     }
567: 
568:   /* User data buffer points (sink) */
569: 
570:   sample = (FAR struct touch_sample_s *)buffer;
571:   point  = sample->point;
572: 
573:   /* Return the number of touches read */
574: 
575:   sample->npoints = ntouches;
576: 
577:   /* Decode and return the touch points */
578: 
579:   for (i = 0; i < ntouches; i++)
580:     {
581:       int event         = TOUCH_POINT_GET_EVENT(touch[i]);
582: 
583:       point[i].id       = TOUCH_POINT_GET_ID(touch[i]);
584:       point[i].flags    = g_event_map[event];
585: #ifdef CONFIG_FT5X06_SWAPXY
586:       point[i].y        = TOUCH_POINT_GET_X(touch[i]);
587:       point[i].x        = TOUCH_POINT_GET_Y(touch[i]);
588: #else
589:       point[i].x        = TOUCH_POINT_GET_X(touch[i]);
590:       point[i].y        = TOUCH_POINT_GET_Y(touch[i]);
591: #endif
592:       point[i].h        = 0;
593:       point[i].w        = 0;
594:       point[i].pressure = 0;
595:     }
596: 
597:   priv->valid = false;
598:   return SIZEOF_TOUCH_SAMPLE_S(ntouches);
599: }
600: #endif /* CONFIG_FT5X06_SINGLEPOINT */

602: /****************************************************************************
603:  * Name: ft5x06_waitsample
604:  ****************************************************************************/
605: 
606: static ssize_t ft5x06_waitsample(FAR struct ft5x06_dev_s *priv,
607:                                  FAR char *buffer, size_t len)
608: {
609:   int ret;
610: 
611:   /* Now release the semaphore that manages mutually exclusive access to
612:    * the device structure.  This may cause other tasks to become ready to
613:    * run, but they cannot run yet because pre-emption is disabled.
614:    */
615: 
616:   nxmutex_unlock(&priv->devlock);
617: 
618:   /* Try to get the a sample... if we cannot, then wait on the semaphore
619:    * that is posted when new sample data is available.
620:    */
621: 
622:   while (!priv->valid)
623:     {
624:       /* Increment the count of waiters */
625: 
626:       priv->nwaiters++;
627: 
628:       /* Wait for a change in the FT5x06 state */
629: 
630:       ret = nxsem_wait(&priv->waitsem);
631:       priv->nwaiters--;
632: 
633:       if (ret < 0)
634:         {
635:           ierr("ERROR: nxsem_wait failed: %d\n", ret);
636:           goto errout;
637:         }
638:     }
639: 
640:   /* Re-acquire the semaphore that manages mutually exclusive access to
641:    * the device structure.  We may have to wait here.  But we have our
642:    * sample.  Interrupts and pre-emption will be re-enabled while we wait.
643:    */
644: 
645:   ret = nxmutex_lock(&priv->devlock);
646:   if (ret >= 0)
647:     {
648:       /* Now sample the data.
649:        *
650:        * REVISIT:  Is it safe to assume that priv->valid will always be
651:        * true?  I think that sched_lock() would protect the setting.
652:        */
653: 
654:       ret = ft5x06_sample(priv, buffer, len);
655:     }
656: 
657: errout:
658:   return ret;
659: }

661: /****************************************************************************
662:  * Name: ft5x06_bringup
663:  ****************************************************************************/
664: 
665: static int ft5x06_bringup(FAR struct ft5x06_dev_s *priv)
666: {
667:   FAR const struct ft5x06_config_s *config;
668:   struct i2c_msg_s msg;
669:   uint8_t data[2];
670:   int ret;
671: 
672:   /* Get a pointer the callbacks for convenience (and so the code is not so
673:    * ugly).
674:    */
675: 
676:   config = priv->config;
677:   DEBUGASSERT(config != NULL);
678: 
679:   /* Set device mode to normal operation */
680: 
681:   data[0]       = FT5X06_TOUCH_MODE_REG;   /* Register address */
682:   data[1]       = FT5X06_DEV_MODE_WORKING; /* Normal mode */
683: 
684:   msg.frequency = priv->frequency;         /* I2C frequency */
685:   msg.addr      = config->address;         /* 7-bit address */
686:   msg.flags     = 0;                       /* Write transaction with START */
687:   msg.buffer    = data;                    /* Send two bytes followed by STOP */
688:   msg.length    = 2;
689: 
690:   ret = I2C_TRANSFER(priv->i2c, &msg, 1);
691:   if (ret < 0)
692:     {
693:       return ret;
694:     }
695: 
696: #ifndef CONFIG_FT5X06_POLLMODE
697:   /* Enable FT5x06 interrupts */
698: 
699:   config->clear(config);
700:   config->enable(config, true);
701: #endif
702:   return OK;
703: }

726: /****************************************************************************
727:  * Name: ft5x06_open
728:  ****************************************************************************/
729: 
730: static int ft5x06_open(FAR struct file *filep)
731: {
732:   FAR struct inode *inode;
733:   FAR struct ft5x06_dev_s *priv;
734:   uint8_t tmp;
735:   int ret;
736: 
737:   inode = filep->f_inode;
738: 
739:   DEBUGASSERT(inode->i_private);
740:   priv  = inode->i_private;
741: 
742:   /* Get exclusive access to the driver data structure */
743: 
744:   ret = nxmutex_lock(&priv->devlock);
745:   if (ret < 0)
746:     {
747:       ierr("ERROR: nxmutex_lock failed: %d\n", ret);
748:       return ret;
749:     }
750: 
751:   /* Increment the reference count */
752: 
753:   tmp = priv->crefs + 1;
754:   if (tmp == 0)
755:     {
756:       /* More than 255 opens; uint8_t overflows to zero */
757: 
758:       ret = -EMFILE;
759:       goto errout_with_lock;
760:     }
761: 
762:   /* When the reference increments to 1, this is the first open event
763:    * on the driver.. and the time when we must initialize the driver.
764:    */
765: 
766:   if (tmp == 1)
767:     {
768:       ret = ft5x06_bringup(priv);
769:       if (ret < 0)
770:         {
771:           ierr("ERROR: ft5x06_bringup failed: %d\n", ret);
772:           goto errout_with_lock;
773:         }
774:     }
775: 
776:   /* Save the new open count on success */
777: 
778:   priv->crefs = tmp;
779: 
780: errout_with_lock:
781:   nxmutex_unlock(&priv->devlock);
782:   return ret;
783: }
784: 
785: /****************************************************************************
786:  * Name: ft5x06_close
787:  ****************************************************************************/
788: 
789: static int ft5x06_close(FAR struct file *filep)
790: {
791:   FAR struct inode *inode;
792:   FAR struct ft5x06_dev_s *priv;
793:   int ret;
794: 
795:   inode = filep->f_inode;
796: 
797:   DEBUGASSERT(inode->i_private);
798:   priv  = inode->i_private;
799: 
800:   /* Get exclusive access to the driver data structure */
801: 
802:   ret = nxmutex_lock(&priv->devlock);
803:   if (ret < 0)
804:     {
805:       ierr("ERROR: nxmutex_lock failed: %d\n", ret);
806:       return ret;
807:     }
808: 
809:   /* Decrement the reference count unless it would decrement a negative
810:    * value.
811:    */
812: 
813:   if (priv->crefs >= 1)
814:     {
815:       priv->crefs--;
816:     }
817: 
818:   /* When the count decrements to zero, there are no further open references
819:    * to the driver and it can be uninitialized.
820:    */
821: 
822:   if (priv->crefs == 0)
823:     {
824:       ft5x06_shutdown(priv);
825:     }
826: 
827:   nxmutex_unlock(&priv->devlock);
828:   return OK;
829: }

831: /****************************************************************************
832:  * Name: ft5x06_read
833:  ****************************************************************************/
834: 
835: static ssize_t ft5x06_read(FAR struct file *filep, FAR char *buffer,
836:                            size_t len)
837: {
838:   FAR struct inode *inode;
839:   FAR struct ft5x06_dev_s *priv;
840:   int ret;
841: 
842:   inode = filep->f_inode;
843: 
844:   DEBUGASSERT(inode->i_private);
845:   priv  = inode->i_private;
846: 
847:   /* Verify that the caller has provided a buffer large enough to receive
848:    * the touch data.
849:    */
850: 
851:   if (len < SIZEOF_TOUCH_SAMPLE_S(1))
852:     {
853:       /* We could provide logic to break up a touch report into segments and
854:        * handle smaller reads... but why?
855:        */
856: 
857:       return -ENOSYS;
858:     }
859: 
860:   /* Get exclusive access to the driver data structure */
861: 
862:   ret = nxmutex_lock(&priv->devlock);
863:   if (ret < 0)
864:     {
865:       ierr("ERROR: nxmutex_lock failed: %d\n", ret);
866:       return ret;
867:     }
868: 
869:   /* Try to read sample data. */
870: 
871:   ret = ft5x06_sample(priv, buffer, len);
872:   while (ret == 0)
873:     {
874:       /* Sample data is not available now.  We would have to wait to receive
875:        * sample data.  If the user has specified the O_NONBLOCK option, then
876:        * just return an error.
877:        */
878: 
879:       if (filep->f_oflags & O_NONBLOCK)
880:         {
881:           ret = -EAGAIN;
882:           goto errout;
883:         }
884: 
885:       /* Wait for sample data */
886: 
887:       ret = ft5x06_waitsample(priv, buffer, len);
888:       if (ret < 0)
889:         {
890:           /* We might have been awakened by a signal */
891: 
892:           goto errout;
893:         }
894:     }
895: 
896:   ret = SIZEOF_TOUCH_SAMPLE_S(1);
897: 
898: errout:
899:   nxmutex_unlock(&priv->devlock);
900:   return ret;
901: }

904:  * Name: ft5x06_ioctl
905:  ****************************************************************************/
906: 
907: static int ft5x06_ioctl(FAR struct file *filep, int cmd, unsigned long arg)
908: {
909:   FAR struct inode        *inode;
910:   FAR struct ft5x06_dev_s *priv;
911:   int                      ret;
912: 
913:   iinfo("cmd: %d arg: %ld\n", cmd, arg);
914:   inode = filep->f_inode;
915: 
916:   DEBUGASSERT(inode->i_private);
917:   priv  = inode->i_private;
918: 
919:   /* Get exclusive access to the driver data structure */
920: 
921:   ret = nxmutex_lock(&priv->devlock);
922:   if (ret < 0)
923:     {
924:       ierr("ERROR: nxmutex_lock failed: %d\n", ret);
925:       return ret;
926:     }
927: 
928:   /* Process the IOCTL by command */
929: 
930:   switch (cmd)
931:     {
932:       case TSIOC_SETFREQUENCY:  /* arg: Pointer to uint32_t frequency value */
933:         {
934:           FAR uint32_t *ptr = (FAR uint32_t *)((uintptr_t)arg);
935:           DEBUGASSERT(priv->config != NULL && ptr != NULL);
936:           priv->frequency = *ptr;
937:         }
938:         break;
939: 
940:       case TSIOC_GETFREQUENCY:  /* arg: Pointer to uint32_t frequency value */
941:         {
942:           FAR uint32_t *ptr = (FAR uint32_t *)((uintptr_t)arg);
943:           DEBUGASSERT(priv->config != NULL && ptr != NULL);
944:           *ptr = priv->frequency;
945:         }
946:         break;
947: 
948:       default:
949:         ret = -ENOTTY;
950:         break;
951:     }
952: 
953:   nxmutex_unlock(&priv->devlock);
954:   return ret;
955: }

957: /****************************************************************************
958:  * Name: ft5x06_poll
959:  ****************************************************************************/
960: 
961: static int ft5x06_poll(FAR struct file *filep, FAR struct pollfd *fds,
962:                        bool setup)
963: {
964:   FAR struct inode        *inode;
965:   FAR struct ft5x06_dev_s *priv;
966:   int                      ret;
967:   int                      i;
968: 
969:   iinfo("setup: %d\n", (int)setup);
970:   DEBUGASSERT(fds);
971:   inode = filep->f_inode;
972: 
973:   DEBUGASSERT(inode->i_private);
974:   priv  = inode->i_private;
975: 
976:   /* Are we setting up the poll?  Or tearing it down? */
977: 
978:   ret = nxmutex_lock(&priv->devlock);
979:   if (ret < 0)
980:     {
981:       ierr("ERROR: nxmutex_lock failed: %d\n", ret);
982:       return ret;
983:     }
984: 
985:   if (setup)
986:     {
987:       /* Ignore waits that do not include POLLIN */
988: 
989:       if ((fds->events & POLLIN) == 0)
990:         {
991:           ierr("ERROR: Missing POLLIN: revents: %08" PRIx32 "\n",
992:                fds->revents);
993:           ret = -EDEADLK;
994:           goto errout;
995:         }
996: 
997:       /* This is a request to set up the poll.  Find an available
998:        * slot for the poll structure reference
999:        */
1000: 
1001:       for (i = 0; i < CONFIG_FT5X06_NPOLLWAITERS; i++)
1002:         {
1003:           /* Find an available slot */
1004: 
1005:           if (!priv->fds[i])
1006:             {
1007:               /* Bind the poll structure and this slot */
1008: 
1009:               priv->fds[i] = fds;
1010:               fds->priv    = &priv->fds[i];
1011:               break;
1012:             }
1013:         }
1014: 
1015:       if (i >= CONFIG_FT5X06_NPOLLWAITERS)
1016:         {
1017:           ierr("ERROR: No available slot found: %d\n", i);
1018:           fds->priv = NULL;
1019:           ret       = -EBUSY;
1020:           goto errout;
1021:         }
1022: 
1023:       /* Should we immediately notify on any of the requested events? */
1024: 
1025:       if (priv->valid)
1026:         {
1027:           poll_notify(&fds, 1, POLLIN);
1028:         }
1029:     }
1030:   else if (fds->priv)
1031:     {
1032:       /* This is a request to tear down the poll. */
1033: 
1034:       FAR struct pollfd **slot = (FAR struct pollfd **)fds->priv;
1035:       DEBUGASSERT(slot != NULL);
1036: 
1037:       /* Remove all memory of the poll setup */
1038: 
1039:       *slot     = NULL;
1040:       fds->priv = NULL;
1041:     }
1042: 
1043: errout:
1044:   nxmutex_unlock(&priv->devlock);
1045:   return ret;
1046: }

1056: /****************************************************************************
1057:  * Name: ft5x06_register
1058:  *
1059:  * Description:
1060:  *   Configure the FT5x06 to use the provided I2C device instance.  This
1061:  *   will register the driver as /dev/inputN where N is the minor device
1062:  *   number
1063:  *
1064:  * Input Parameters:
1065:  *   dev     - An I2C driver instance
1066:  *   config  - Persistent board configuration data
1067:  *   minor   - The input device minor number
1068:  *
1069:  * Returned Value:
1070:  *   Zero is returned on success.  Otherwise, a negated errno value is
1071:  *   returned to indicate the nature of the failure.
1072:  *
1073:  ****************************************************************************/
1074: 
1075: int ft5x06_register(FAR struct i2c_master_s *i2c,
1076:                     FAR const struct ft5x06_config_s *config, int minor)
1077: {
1078:   FAR struct ft5x06_dev_s *priv;
1079:   char devname[DEV_NAMELEN];
1080:   int ret;
1081: 
1082:   iinfo("i2c: %p minor: %d\n", i2c, minor);
1083: 
1084:   /* Debug-only sanity checks */
1085: 
1086:   DEBUGASSERT(i2c != NULL && config != NULL && minor >= 0 && minor < 100);

248: static int touch_ioctl(FAR struct file *filep, int cmd, unsigned long arg)

264:           if (enable)
265:             {
266:               if (upper->grab != NULL)
267:                 {
268:                   ret = -EBUSY;
269:                 }
270:               else
271:                 {
272:                   upper->grab = openpriv;
273:                 }
274:             }
275:           else
276:             {
277:               if (upper->grab != openpriv)
278:                 {
279:                   ret = -EINVAL;
280:                 }
281:               else
282:                 {
283:                   upper->grab = NULL;
284:                 }
285:             }
286:         }
287:         break;
288:       case TSIOC_GETMAXPOINTS:
289:         {
290:           if (arg == 0)
291:             {
292:               ret = -EINVAL;

297:           *ptr = lower->maxpoint;

299:         break;
300:       default:
301:         {
302:           if (lower->control)
303:             {
304:               ret = lower->control(lower, cmd, arg);
305:             }
306:           else
307:             {
308:               ret = -ENOTTY;
309:             }
310:         }
311:         break;
312:     }
313: 
314:   spin_unlock_irqrestore(&upper->lock, flags);
315:   return ret;

326:   pollevent_t eventset = 0;
327:   irqstate_t flags;
328:   int ret = OK;
329: 
330:   flags = spin_lock_irqsave_nopreempt(&openpriv->lock);
331: 
332:   if (setup)
333:     {
334:       if (openpriv->fds == NULL)
335:         {
336:           openpriv->fds = fds;
337:           fds->priv     = &openpriv->fds;
338:         }
339:       else
340:         {
341:           ret = -EBUSY;
342:           goto errout;
343:         }
344: 
345:       if (!circbuf_is_empty(&openpriv->circbuf))
346:         {
347:           eventset |= POLLIN;
348:         }
349: 
350:       poll_notify(&fds, 1, eventset);
351:     }
352:   else if (fds->priv)
353:     {
354:       openpriv->fds = NULL;
355:       fds->priv     = NULL;
356:     }
357: 
358: errout:
359:   spin_unlock_irqrestore_nopreempt(&openpriv->lock, flags);
360:   return ret;
361: }

543: /****************************************************************************
544:  * Name: mxt_flushmsgs
545:  *
546:  *   Clear any pending messages be reading messages until there are no
547:  *   pending messages.  This will force the CHG pin to the high state and
548:  *   prevent spurious initial interrupts.
549:  *
550:  ****************************************************************************/
551: 
552: static int mxt_flushmsgs(FAR struct mxt_dev_s *priv)
553: {
554:   struct mxt_msg_s msg;
555:   int retries = 16;
556:   int ret;
557: 
558:   /* Read dummy message until there are no more to read (or until we have
559:    * tried 10 times).
560:    */
561: 
562:   do
563:     {
564:       ret = mxt_getmessage(priv, &msg);
565:       if (ret < 0)
566:         {
567:           ierr("ERROR: mxt_getmessage failed: %d\n", ret);
568:           return ret;
569:         }
570:     }
571:   while (msg.id != 0xff && --retries > 0);
572: 
573:   /* Complain if we exceed the retry limit */
574: 
575:   if (retries <= 0)
576:     {
577:       ierr("ERROR: Failed to clear messages: ID=%02x\n", msg.id);
578:       return -EBUSY;
579:     }
580: 
581:   return OK;
582: }

584: /****************************************************************************
585:  * Name: mxt_notify
586:  ****************************************************************************/
587: 
588: static void mxt_notify(FAR struct mxt_dev_s *priv)
589: {
590:   /* If there are threads waiting on poll() for maXTouch data to become
591:    * available, then wake them up now.  NOTE: we wake up all waiting threads
592:    * because we do not know that they are going to do.  If they all try to
593:    * read the data, then some make end up blocking after all.
594:    */
595: 
596:   poll_notify(priv->fds, CONFIG_MXT_NPOLLWAITERS, POLLIN);
597: 
598:   /* If there are threads waiting for read data, then signal one of them
599:    * that the read data is available.
600:    */
601: 
602:   if (priv->nwaiters > 0)
603:     {
604:       /* After posting this semaphore, we need to exit because the maXTouch
605:        * is no longer available.
606:        */
607: 
608:       nxsem_post(&priv->waitsem);
609:     }
610: }
611: 
612: /****************************************************************************
613:  * Name: mxt_checksample
614:  *
615:  * Description:
616:  *   This function implements a test and clear of the priv->event flag.
617:  *   Called only from mxt_waitsample.
618:  *
619:  * Assumptions:
620:  *   - Scheduler must be locked to prevent the worker thread from running
621:  *     while this thread runs.  The sample data is, of course, updated from
622:  *     the worker thread.
623:  *  -  Interrupts must be disabled when this is called to (1) prevent posting
624:  *     of semaphores from interrupt handlers, and (2) to prevent sampled data
625:  *     from changing until it has been reported.
626:  *
627:  ****************************************************************************/
628: 
629: static inline int mxt_checksample(FAR struct mxt_dev_s *priv)
630: {
631:   /* Is there new maXTouch sample data available? */
632: 
633:   if (priv->event)
634:     {
635:       /* Yes.. clear the flag and return success */
636: 
637:       priv->event = false;
638:       return OK;
639:     }
640: 
641:   /* No.. return failure */
642: 
643:   return -EAGAIN;
644: }
645: 
646: /****************************************************************************
647:  * Name: mxt_waitsample
648:  *
649:  * Wait until sample data is available.  Called only from mxt_read.
650:  *
651:  * Assumptions:
652:  *   - Scheduler must be locked to prevent the worker thread from running
653:  *     while this thread runs.  The sample data is, of course, updated from
654:  *     the worker thread.
655:  *
656:  ****************************************************************************/
657: 
658: static inline int mxt_waitsample(FAR struct mxt_dev_s *priv)
659: {
660:   irqstate_t flags;
661:   int ret;
662: 
663:   /* Interrupts must be disabled when this is called to (1) prevent posting
664:    * of semaphores from interrupt handlers, and (2) to prevent sampled data
665:    * from changing until it has been reported.
666:    */
667: 
668:   flags = enter_critical_section();
669: 
670:   /* Now release the semaphore that manages mutually exclusive access to
671:    * the device structure.  This may cause other tasks to become ready to
672:    * run, but they cannot run yet because pre-emption is disabled.
673:    */
674: 
675:   nxmutex_unlock(&priv->devlock);
676: 
677:   /* Try to get the a sample... if we cannot, then wait on the semaphore
678:    * that is posted when new sample data is available.
679:    */
680: 
681:   while (mxt_checksample(priv) < 0)
682:     {
683:       /* Wait for a change in the maXTouch state */
684: 
685:       priv->nwaiters++;
686:       ret = nxsem_wait(&priv->waitsem);
687:       priv->nwaiters--;
688: 
689:       if (ret < 0)
690:         {
691:           goto errout;
692:         }
693:     }
694: 
695:   /* Re-acquire the semaphore that manages mutually exclusive access to
696:    * the device structure.  We may have to wait here.  But we have our
697:    * sample.  Interrupts and pre-emption will be re-enabled while we wait.
698:    */
699: 
700:   ret = nxmutex_lock(&priv->devlock);
701: 
702: errout:
703:   /* Then re-enable interrupts.  We might get interrupt here and there
704:    * could be a new sample.  But no new threads will run because we still
705:    * have pre-emption disabled.
706:    */
707: 
708:   leave_critical_section(flags);
709:   return ret;
710: }

753: 
754: static void mxt_touch_event(FAR struct mxt_dev_s *priv,
755:                             FAR struct mxt_msg_s *msg, int ndx)
756: {
757:   FAR struct mxt_sample_s *sample;
758:   uint16_t x;
759:   uint16_t y;
760:   uint8_t  area;
761:   uint8_t  pressure;
762:   uint8_t  status;
763: 
764:   /* Extract the 12-bit X and Y positions */
765: 
766:   x = ((uint16_t)msg->body[1] << 4) |
767:       (((uint16_t)msg->body[3] >> 4) & 0x0f);
768:   y = ((uint16_t)msg->body[2] << 4) |
769:       (((uint16_t)msg->body[3] & 0x0f));
770: 
771:   /* Swap X/Y as necessary */
772: 
773:   if (priv->lower->swapxy)
774:     {
775:       uint16_t tmp = x;
776:       y = x;
777:       x = tmp;
778:     }
779: 
780:   /* Extract area pressure and status */
781: 
782:   area     = msg->body[4];
783:   pressure = msg->body[5];
784: 
785:   status = msg->body[0];
786:   iinfo("ndx=%u status=%02x pos(%u,%u) area=%u pressure=%u\n",
787:         ndx, status, x, y, area, pressure);
788: 
789:   /* The normal sequence that we would see for a touch would be something
790:    * like:
791:    *
792:    *   1. MXT_DETECT + MXT_PRESS
793:    *   2. MXT_DETECT + MXT_AMP
794:    *   3. MXT_DETECT + MXT_MOVE + MXT_AMP
795:    *   4. MXT_RELEASE
796:    *
797:    * So we really only need to check MXT_DETECT to drive this state machine.
798:    */
799: 
800:   /* Is this a loss of contact? */
801: 
802:   sample = &priv->sample[ndx];
803:   if ((status & MXT_DETECT) == 0)
804:     {
805:       /* Ignore the event if there was no contact to be lost:
806:        *
807:        *   CONTACT_NONE = No touch and loss-of-contact already reported
808:        *   CONTACT_LOST = No touch and unreported loss-of-contact.
809:        */
810: 
811:       if (sample->contact == CONTACT_NONE)
812:         {
813:           /* Return without posting any event */
814: 
815:           return;
816:         }
817: 
818:       /* State is one of CONTACT_NEW, CONTACT_MOVE, CONTACT_REPORT or
819:        * CONTACT_LOST.
820:        *
821:        * NOTE: Here we do not check for these other states because there is
822:        * not much that can be done anyway.  The transition to CONTACK_LOST
823:        * really only makes sense if the preceding state was CONTACT_REPORT.
824:        * If we were in (unreported) CONTACT_NEW or CONTACT_MOVE states, then
825:        * this will overwrite that event and it will not be reported.  This
826:        * opens the possibility for contact lost reports when no contact was
827:        * ever reported.
828:        *
829:        * We could improve this be leaving the unreported states in place,
830:        * remembering that the contact was lost, and then reporting the loss-
831:        * of-contact after touch state is reported.
832:        */
833: 
834:       sample->contact = CONTACT_LOST;
835: 
836:       /* Reset the last position so that we guarantee that the next position
837:        * will pass the thresholding test.
838:        */
839: 
840:       sample->lastx = INVALID_POSITION;
841:       sample->lasty = INVALID_POSITION;
842:     }
843:   else
844:     {
845:       /* It is a touch event.  If the last loss-of-contact event has not
846:        * been processed yet, then have to bump up the touch identifier and
847:        * hope that the client is smart enough to infer the loss-of-contact
848:        * event for the preceding touch.
849:        */
850: 
851:       if (sample->contact == CONTACT_LOST)
852:         {
853:            priv->id++;
854:         }
855: 
856:       /* Save the measurements */
857: 
858:       sample->x        = x;
859:       sample->y        = y;
860:       sample->area     = area;
861:       sample->pressure = pressure;
862:       sample->valid    = true;
863: 
864:       add_ui_randomness((x << 16) ^ y ^ (area << 9) ^ (pressure << 1));
865: 
866:       /* If this is not the first touch report, then report it as a move:
867:        * Same contact, same ID, but with a new, updated position.
868:        * The CONTACT_REPORT state means that a contacted has been detected,
869:        * but all contact events have been successfully reported.
870:        */
871: 
872:       if (sample->contact == CONTACT_REPORT)
873:         {
874:           uint16_t xdiff;
875:           uint16_t ydiff;
876: 
877:           /* Not a new contact.  Check if the new measurements represent a
878:            * non-trivial change in position.  A trivial change is detected
879:            * by comparing the change in position since the last report
880:            * against configurable threshold values.
881:            *
882:            * REVISIT:  Should a large change in pressure also generate a
883:            * event?
884:            */
885: 
886:           xdiff = x > sample->lastx ? (x - sample->lastx) :
887:                                       (sample->lastx - x);
888:           ydiff = y > sample->lasty ? (y - sample->lasty) :
889:                                       (sample->lasty - y);
890: 
891:           /* Check the thresholds */
892: 
893:           if (xdiff >= CONFIG_MXT_THRESHX || ydiff >= CONFIG_MXT_THRESHY)
894:             {
895:               /* Report a contact move event.  This state will be set back
896:                * to CONTACT_REPORT after it been reported.
897:                */
898: 
899:               sample->contact = CONTACT_MOVE;
900: 
901:               /* Update the last position for next threshold calculations */
902: 
903:               sample->lastx   = x;
904:               sample->lasty   = y;
905:             }
906:           else
907:             {
908:               /* Bail without reporting anything for this event */
909: 
910:               return;
911:             }
912:         }
913: 
914:       /* If we have seen this contact before but it has not yet been
915:        * reported, then do nothing other than overwrite the positional
916:        * data.
917:        *
918:        * This the state must be one of CONTACT_NONE or CONTACT_LOST (see
919:        * above) and we have a new contact with a new ID.
920:        */
921: 
922:       else if (sample->contact != CONTACT_NEW &&
923:                sample->contact != CONTACT_MOVE)
924:         {
925:           /* First contact.  Save the contact event and assign a new
926:            * ID to the contact.
927:            */
928: 
929:           sample->contact = CONTACT_NEW;
930:           sample->id      = priv->id++;
931: 
932:           /* Update the last position for next threshold calculations */
933: 
934:           sample->lastx   = x;
935:           sample->lasty   = y;
936: 
937:           /* This state will be set to CONTACT_REPORT after it
938:            * been reported.
939:            */
940:         }
941:     }
942: 
943:   /* Indicate the availability of new sample data for this ID and notify
944:    * any waiters that new maXTouch data is available
945:    */
946: 
947:   priv->event = true;
948:   mxt_notify(priv);
949: }

951: /****************************************************************************
952:  * Name: mxt_worker
953:  ****************************************************************************/
954: 
955: static void mxt_worker(FAR void *arg)
956: {
957:   FAR struct mxt_dev_s *priv = (FAR struct mxt_dev_s *)arg;
958:   FAR const struct mxt_lower_s *lower;
959:   struct mxt_msg_s msg;
960:   uint8_t id;
961:   int retries;
962:   int ret;
963: 
964:   DEBUGASSERT(priv != NULL);
965: 
966:   /* Get a pointer the callbacks for convenience (and so the code is not so
967:    * ugly).
968:    */
969: 
970:   lower = priv->lower;
971:   DEBUGASSERT(lower != NULL);
972: 
973:   /* Get exclusive access to the MXT driver data structure */
974: 
975:   nxmutex_lock(&priv->devlock);
976: 
977:   /* Loop, processing each message from the maXTouch */
978: 
979:   retries = 0;
980:   do
981:     {
982:       /* Retrieve the next message from the maXTouch */
983: 
984:       ret = mxt_getmessage(priv, &msg);
985:       if (ret < 0)
986:         {
987:           ierr("ERROR: mxt_getmessage failed: %d\n", ret);
988:           goto errout_with_lock;
989:         }
990: 
991:       id = msg.id;
992: 
993: #ifdef MXT_SUPPORT_T6
994:       /* Check for T6 */
995: 
996:       if (id == priv->t6id)
997:         {
998:           uint32_t chksum;
999:           int status;
1000: 
1001:           status = msg.body[0];
1002:           chksum = (uint32_t)msg.body[1] |
1003:                   ((uint32_t)msg.body[2] << 8) |
1004:                   ((uint32_t)msg.body[3] << 16);
1005: 
1006:           iinfo("T6: status: %02x checksum: %06lx\n",
1007:                 status, (unsigned long)chksum);
1008: 
1009:           retries = 0;
1010:         }
1011:       else
1012: #endif
1013: 
1014:       /* Check for T9 */
1015: 
1016:       if (id >= priv->t9idmin && id <= priv->t9idmax)
1017:         {
1018:           mxt_touch_event(priv, &msg, id - priv->t9idmin);
1019:           retries = 0;
1020:         }
1021: 
1022: #ifdef CONFIG_MXT_BUTTONS
1023:       /* Check for T19 */
1024: 
1025:       else if (msg.id == priv->t19id)
1026:         {
1027:           mxt_button_event(priv, &msg);
1028:           retries = 0;
1029:         }
1030: #endif
1031: 
1032:       /* 0xff marks the end of the messages; any other message IDs are
1033:        * ignored (after complaining a little).
1034:        */
1035: 
1036:       else if (msg.id != 0xff)
1037:         {
1038:           iinfo("Ignored: id=%u message="
1039:                 "{%02x %02x %02x %02x %02x %02x %02x}\n",
1040:                 msg.id,
1041:                 msg.body[0], msg.body[1], msg.body[2],
1042:                 msg.body[3], msg.body[4], msg.body[5],
1043:                 msg.body[6]);
1044: 
1045:           retries++;
1046:         }
1047:     }
1048:   while (id != 0xff && retries < 16);
1049: 
1050: errout_with_lock:
1051: 
1052:   /* Release our lock on the MXT device */
1053: 
1054:   nxmutex_unlock(&priv->devlock);
1055: 
1056:   /* Acknowledge and re-enable maXTouch interrupts */
1057: 
1058:   MXT_CLEAR(lower);
1059:   MXT_ENABLE(lower);
1060: }

1062: /****************************************************************************
1063:  * Name: mxt_interrupt
1064:  ****************************************************************************/
1065: 
1066: static int mxt_interrupt(FAR const struct mxt_lower_s *lower, FAR void *arg)
1067: {
1068:   FAR struct mxt_dev_s *priv = (FAR struct mxt_dev_s *)arg;
1069:   int ret;
1070: 
1071:   /* Get a pointer the callbacks for convenience (and so the code is not so
1072:    * ugly).
1073:    */
1074: 
1075:   DEBUGASSERT(lower != NULL && priv != NULL);
1076: 
1077:   /* Disable further interrupts */
1078: 
1079:   MXT_DISABLE(lower);
1080: 
1081:   /* Transfer processing to the worker thread.  Since maXTouch interrupts are
1082:    * disabled while the work is pending, no special action should be required
1083:    * to protected the work queue.
1084:    */
1085: 
1086:   DEBUGASSERT(priv->work.worker == NULL);
1087:   ret = work_queue(HPWORK, &priv->work, mxt_worker, priv, 0);
1088:   if (ret != 0)
1089:     {
1090:       ierr("ERROR: Failed to queue work: %d\n", ret);
1091:     }
1092: 
1093:   /* Clear any pending interrupts and return success */
1094: 
1095:   lower->clear(lower);
1096:   return OK;
1097: }

1103: static int mxt_open(FAR struct file *filep)
1104: {
1105:   FAR struct inode *inode;
1106:   FAR struct mxt_dev_s *priv;
1107:   uint8_t tmp;
1108:   int ret;
1109: 
1110:   inode = filep->f_inode;
1111: 
1112:   DEBUGASSERT(inode->i_private);
1113:   priv  = inode->i_private;
1114: 
1115:   /* Get exclusive access to the driver data structure */
1116: 
1117:   ret = nxmutex_lock(&priv->devlock);
1118:   if (ret < 0)
1119:     {
1120:       return ret;
1121:     }
1122: 
1123:   /* Increment the reference count */
1124: 
1125:   tmp = priv->crefs + 1;
1126:   if (tmp == 0)
1127:     {
1128:       /* More than 255 opens; uint8_t overflows to zero */
1129: 
1130:       ierr("ERROR: Too many opens: %d\n", priv->crefs);
1131:       ret = -EMFILE;
1132:       goto errout_with_lock;
1133:     }
1134: 
1135:   /* When the reference increments to 1, this is the first open event
1136:    * on the driver.. and an opportunity to do any one-time initialization.
1137:    */
1138: 
1139:   if (tmp == 1)
1140:     {
1141:       /* Touch enable */
1142: 
1143:       ret = mxt_putobject(priv, MXT_TOUCH_MULTI_T9, MXT_TOUCH_CTRL, 0x83);
1144:       if (ret < 0)
1145:         {
1146:           ierr("ERROR: Failed to enable touch: %d\n", ret);
1147:           goto errout_with_lock;
1148:         }
1149: 
1150:       /* Clear any pending messages by reading all messages.  This will
1151:        * force the CHG interrupt pin to the high state and prevent spurious
1152:        * interrupts when they are enabled.
1153:        */
1154: 
1155:       ret = mxt_flushmsgs(priv);
1156:       if (ret < 0)
1157:         {
1158:           ierr("ERROR: mxt_flushmsgs failed: %d\n", ret);
1159:           mxt_putobject(priv, MXT_TOUCH_MULTI_T9, MXT_TOUCH_CTRL, 0);
1160:           goto errout_with_lock;
1161:         }
1162: 
1163:       /* Enable touch interrupts */
1164: 
1165:       MXT_ENABLE(priv->lower);
1166:     }
1167: 
1168:   /* Save the new open count on success */
1169: 
1170:   priv->crefs = tmp;
1171: 
1172: errout_with_lock:
1173:   nxmutex_unlock(&priv->devlock);
1174:   return ret;
1175: }

139: /****************************************************************************
140:  * Name: stmpe811_notify
141:  *
142:  * Description:
143:  *   Notify any threads waiting on touchscreen data that data is now
144:  *   available for reading.
145:  *
146:  ****************************************************************************/
147: 
148: static void stmpe811_notify(FAR struct stmpe811_dev_s *priv)
149: {
150:   /* If there are threads waiting on poll() for STMPE811 data to become
151:    * available, then wake them up now.  NOTE: we wake up all waiting threads
152:    * because we do not know that they are going to do.  If they all try to
153:    * read the data, then some make end up blocking after all.
154:    */
155: 
156:   poll_notify(priv->fds, CONFIG_STMPE811_NPOLLWAITERS, POLLIN);
157: 
158:   /* If there are threads waiting for read data, then signal one of them
159:    * that the read data is available.
160:    */
161: 
162:   if (priv->nwaiters > 0)
163:     {
164:       /* After posting this semaphore, we need to exit because the STMPE811
165:        * is no longer available.
166:        */
167: 
168:       nxsem_post(&priv->waitsem);
169:     }
170: }

172: /****************************************************************************
173:  * Name: stmpe811_sample
174:  *
175:  * Description:
176:  *   Check if touchscreen sample data is available now and, if so, return
177:  *   the sample data.  This is part of the stmpe811_read logic.
178:  *
179:  * Assumption:
180:  *   Pre-emption is disable to prevent the worker thread from running.
181:  *   Otherwise, sampled data may continue to change.
182:  *
183:  ****************************************************************************/
184: 
185: static int stmpe811_sample(FAR struct stmpe811_dev_s *priv,
186:                            FAR struct stmpe811_sample_s *sample)
187: {
188:   int ret = -EAGAIN;
189: 
190:   /* Is there new STMPE811 sample data available? */
191: 
192:   if (priv->penchange)
193:     {
194:       /* Yes.. the state has changed in some way.  Return a copy of the
195:        * sampled data.
196:        */
197: 
198:       memcpy(sample, &priv->sample, sizeof(struct stmpe811_sample_s));
199: 
200:       /* Now manage state transitions */
201: 
202:       if (sample->contact == CONTACT_UP)
203:         {
204:           /* The sampling logic has detected pen-up in some condition other
205:            * than CONTACT_NONE.  Set the next state to CONTACT_NONE:  Further
206:            * pen-down reports will be ignored.  Increment the ID so that
207:            * next contact ID will be unique
208:            */
209: 
210:           priv->sample.contact = CONTACT_NONE;
211:           priv->sample.valid   = false;
212:           priv->id++;
213:         }
214:       else if (sample->contact == CONTACT_DOWN)
215:         {
216:           /* The sampling logic has detected pen-up in some condition other
217:            * than CONTACT_MOVE. Set the next state to CONTACT_MOVE: Further
218:            * samples collected while the pen is down will reported as
219:            * movement events.
220:            */
221: 
222:          priv->sample.contact = CONTACT_MOVE;
223:         }
224: 
225:       priv->penchange = false;
226:       ret = OK;
227:     }
228: 
229:   return ret;
230: }

232: /****************************************************************************
233:  * Name: stmpe811_waitsample
234:  *
235:  * Description:
236:  *   Wait for a sample to become available (this is really part of the
237:  *   stmpe811_read logic).
238:  *
239:  ****************************************************************************/
240: 
241: static inline int stmpe811_waitsample(FAR struct stmpe811_dev_s *priv,
242:                                       FAR struct stmpe811_sample_s *sample)
243: {
244:   int ret;
245:   irqstate_t flags;
246: 
247:   /* Disable pre-emption to prevent the worker thread from running
248:    * asynchronously.
249:    */
250: 
251:   flags = enter_critical_section();
252: 
253:   /* Now release the semaphore that manages mutually exclusive access to
254:    * the device structure.  This may cause other tasks to become ready to
255:    * run, but they cannot run yet because pre-emption is disabled.
256:    */
257: 
258:   nxmutex_unlock(&priv->lock);
259: 
260:   /* Try to get the a sample... if we cannot, then wait on the semaphore
261:    * that is posted when new sample data is available.
262:    */
263: 
264:   while (stmpe811_sample(priv, sample) < 0)
265:     {
266:       /* Wait for a change in the STMPE811 state */
267: 
268:       priv->nwaiters++;
269:       ret = nxsem_wait(&priv->waitsem);
270:       priv->nwaiters--;
271: 
272:       /* When we are re-awakened, pre-emption will again be disabled */
273: 
274:       if (ret < 0)
275:         {
276:           ierr("ERROR: nxsem_wait failed: %d\n", ret);
277:           goto errout;
278:         }
279:     }
280: 
281:   /* Re-acquire the semaphore that manages mutually exclusive access to
282:    * the device structure. We may have to wait here. But we have our sample.
283:    * Interrupts and pre-emption will be re-enabled while we wait.
284:    */
285: 
286:   ret = nxmutex_lock(&priv->lock);
287: 
288: errout:
289:   /* Then re-enable interrupts.  We might get interrupt here and there
290:    * could be a new sample.  But no new threads will run because we still
291:    * have pre-emption disabled.
292:    */
293: 
294:   leave_critical_section(flags);
295:   return ret;
296: }

624: static int stmpe811_poll(FAR struct file *filep, FAR struct pollfd *fds,
625:                          bool setup)
626: {
627:   FAR struct inode          *inode;
628:   FAR struct stmpe811_dev_s *priv;
