634:   inode = filep->f_inode;
635: 
636:   DEBUGASSERT(inode->i_private);
637:   priv  = inode->i_private;
638: 
639:   /* Are we setting up the poll?  Or tearing it down? */
640: 
641:   ret = nxmutex_lock(&priv->lock);
642:   if (ret < 0)
643:     {
644:       /* This should only happen if the wait was canceled by an signal */
645: 
646:       ierr("ERROR: nxsem_wait failed: %d\n", ret);
647:       return ret;
648:     }
649: 
650:   if (setup)
651:     {
652:       /* Ignore waits that do not include POLLIN */
653: 
654:       if ((fds->events & POLLIN) == 0)
655:         {
656:           ierr("ERROR: Missing POLLIN: revents: %08" PRIx32 "\n",
657:                fds->revents);
658:           ret = -EDEADLK;
659:           goto errout;
660:         }
661: 
662:       /* This is a request to set up the poll.  Find an available
663:        * slot for the poll structure reference
664:        */
665: 
666:       for (i = 0; i < CONFIG_STMPE811_NPOLLWAITERS; i++)
667:         {
668:           /* Find an available slot */
669: 
670:           if (!priv->fds[i])
671:             {
672:               /* Bind the poll structure and this slot */
673: 
674:               priv->fds[i] = fds;
675:               fds->priv    = &priv->fds[i];
676:               break;
677:             }
678:         }
679: 
680:       if (i >= CONFIG_STMPE811_NPOLLWAITERS)
681:         {
682:           ierr("ERROR: No available slot found: %d\n", i);
683:           fds->priv = NULL;
684:           ret       = -EBUSY;
685:           goto errout;
686:         }
687: 
688:       /* Should we immediately notify on any of the requested events? */
689: 
690:       if (priv->penchange)
691:         {
692:           poll_notify(&fds, 1, POLLIN);
693:         }
694:     }
695:   else if (fds->priv)
696:     {
697:       /* This is a request to tear down the poll. */
698: 
699:       FAR struct pollfd **slot = (FAR struct pollfd **)fds->priv;
700:       DEBUGASSERT(slot != NULL);
701: 
702:       /* Remove all memory of the poll setup */
703: 
704:       *slot     = NULL;
705:       fds->priv = NULL;
706:     }
707: 
708: errout:
709:   nxmutex_unlock(&priv->lock);
710:   return ret;
711: }

241: {
242:   /* If there are threads waiting on poll() for TSC2007 data to become
243:    * available, then wake them up now.  NOTE: we wake up all waiting
244:    * threads because we do not know that they are going to do.  If they
245:    * all try to read the data, then some make end up blocking after all.
246:    */

251:    * that the read data is available.
252:    */
253: 
254:   if (priv->nwaiters > 0)
255:     {
256:       /* After posting this semaphore, we need to exit because the TSC2007
257:        * is no longer available.
258:        */
259: 
260:       nxsem_post(&priv->waitsem);
261:     }

264: /****************************************************************************
265:  * Name: tsc2007_sample
266:  ****************************************************************************/
267: 
268: static int tsc2007_sample(FAR struct tsc2007_dev_s *priv,
269:                           FAR struct tsc2007_sample_s *sample)
270: {
271:   irqstate_t flags;
272:   int ret = -EAGAIN;
273: 
274:   /* Interrupts must be disabled when this is called to (1) prevent posting
275:    * of semaphores from interrupt handlers, and (2) to prevent sampled data
276:    * from changing until it has been reported.
277:    */
278: 
279:   flags = enter_critical_section();
280: 
281:   /* Is there new TSC2007 sample data available? */
282: 
283:   if (priv->penchange)
284:     {
285:       /* Yes.. the state has changed in some way.  Return a copy of the
286:        * sampled data.
287:        */
288: 
289:       memcpy(sample, &priv->sample, sizeof(struct tsc2007_sample_s));
290: 
291:       /* Now manage state transitions */
292: 
293:       if (sample->contact == CONTACT_UP)
294:         {
295:           /* Next.. no contact.  Increment the ID so that next contact ID
296:            * will be unique.  X/Y positions are no longer valid.
297:            */
298: 
299:           priv->sample.contact = CONTACT_NONE;
300:           priv->sample.valid   = false;
301:           priv->id++;
302:         }
303:       else if (sample->contact == CONTACT_DOWN)
304:         {
305:           /* First report -- next report will be a movement */
306: 
307:           priv->sample.contact = CONTACT_MOVE;
308:         }
309: 
310:       priv->penchange = false;
311:       ret = OK;
312:     }
313: 
314:   leave_critical_section(flags);
315:   return ret;
316: }

318: /****************************************************************************
319:  * Name: tsc2007_waitsample
320:  ****************************************************************************/
321: 
322: static int tsc2007_waitsample(FAR struct tsc2007_dev_s *priv,
323:                               FAR struct tsc2007_sample_s *sample)
324: {
325:   irqstate_t flags;
326:   int ret;
327: 
328:   /* Interrupts must be disabled when this is called to (1) prevent posting
329:    * of semaphores from interrupt handlers, and (2) to prevent sampled data
330:    * from changing until it has been reported.
331:    *
332:    * In addition, we will also disable pre-emption to prevent other threads
333:    * from getting control while we muck with the semaphores.
334:    */
335: 
336:   flags = enter_critical_section();
337: 
338:   /* Now release the semaphore that manages mutually exclusive access to
339:    * the device structure.  This may cause other tasks to become ready to
340:    * run, but they cannot run yet because pre-emption is disabled.
341:    */
342: 
343:   nxmutex_unlock(&priv->devlock);
344: 
345:   /* Try to get the a sample... if we cannot, then wait on the semaphore
346:    * that is posted when new sample data is available.
347:    */
348: 
349:   while (tsc2007_sample(priv, sample) < 0)
350:     {
351:       /* Wait for a change in the TSC2007 state */
352: 
353:       priv->nwaiters++;
354:       ret = nxsem_wait(&priv->waitsem);
355:       priv->nwaiters--;
356: 
357:       if (ret < 0)
358:         {
359:           ierr("ERROR: nxsem_wait failed: %d\n", ret);
360:           goto errout;
361:         }
362:     }
363: 
364:   /* Re-acquire the semaphore that manages mutually exclusive access to
365:    * the device structure.  We may have to wait here.  But we have our
366:    * sample.  Interrupts and pre-emption will be re-enabled while we wait.
367:    */
368: 
369:   ret = nxmutex_lock(&priv->devlock);
370: 
371: errout:
372:   /* Then re-enable interrupts.  We might get interrupt here and there
373:    * could be a new sample.  But no new threads will run because we still
374:    * have pre-emption disabled.
375:    */
376: 
377:   leave_critical_section(flags);
378:   return ret;
379: }

      "message": "input/gt9xx: fix register write and no-contact read\n\nTwo defects keep the driver from reporting touches on a board that\ncannot use the interrupt line.\n\nThe register write built two messages joined by I2C_M_NOSTART.  That\nputs the same bytes on the wire as a single three byte message, but\nresuming a transfer without a start condition is optional, and a\ncontroller that does not implement it fails the transfer.  On the\nESP32-P4 every write returned -ETIMEDOUT, so the buffer status clear\nat 0x814E never reached the controller and gt9xx_read_touch_data()\nreturned an error for every read.  Send the register address and the\nvalue as a single message.\n\nread() returned a full struct touch_sample_s even when the controller\nreported no contact, with npoints set to zero.  A caller that judges\nthe read by its return value takes that for valid data: the LVGL\ntouchscreen driver reads a second sample to decide whether to keep\nreading, always gets one, so it sets continue_reading on every pass\nand lv_indev_read() never returns.  The display then stops refreshing\nafter the first frame while the touch reads spin.  Return -EAGAIN when\nthere is no contact and the file was opened with O_NONBLOCK, which is\nwhat the touchscreen upper half does in the same situation.  A\nblocking reader keeps the previous behaviour.\n\nWhile here, add the blank line after the declaration in gt9xx_poll() that\nnxstyle asks for.  It predates this change, but the CI runs checkpatch over\nevery file a commit touches, so it has to go.\n\nSigned-off-by: Jorge Guzman <jorge.gzm@gmail.com>",

      "message": "drivers/: Multiple Drivers Are Registered With World Writable - Part 2\n\nPermissions (Part 2)\n\nDescription:\n\nIn kernel builds, any unprivileged process running on the NuttX\ndevice can open /dev/efuse and attempt to read/write fuse content.\nReading the fuses may provide valuable information to an attacker\ncontrolling the user process. The write operation, in extreme cases\nwhere the fuse blocks are not locked, may brick the device.\n\nDISCLAIMER: I tried to be strict with the settings, better to relax them\nlater if it's needed.\n\nThis is part of https://github.com/apache/nuttx/issues/19410\n\nSee https://github.com/apache/nuttx/issues/19410\n\nCompiles ok.\n\nSigned-off-by: Catalin Visinescu <catalin_visinescu@yahoo.com>",

      "message": "include/debug.h: Move to include/nuttx/debug.h\n\ndebug.h is a NuttX-specific, non-POSIX header. Placing it in the\ntop-level include/ directory creates naming conflicts with external\nprojects that define their own debug.h.\nThis commit moves the canonical header to include/nuttx/debug.h,\nfollowing the NuttX convention for non-POSIX/non-standard headers,\nand updates all in-tree references.\n\nA backward-compatibility shim is left at include/debug.h that\nemits a deprecation #warning and re-includes <nuttx/debug.h>,\nallowing out-of-tree code to continue building while migrating.\n\nSigned-off-by: Piyush Patle <piyushpatle228@gmail.com>",

      "message": "sched/sleep: replace all Signal-based sleep implement to Scheduled sleep\n\nNuttx currently has 2 types of sleep interfaces:\n\n1. Signal-scheduled sleep: nxsig_sleep() / nxsig_usleep() / nxsig_nanosleep()\nWeaknesses:\na. Signal-dependent: The signal-scheduled sleep method is bound to the signal framework, while some driver sleep operations do not depend on signals.\nb. Timespec conversion: Signal-scheduled sleep involves timespec conversion, which has a significant impact on performance.\n\n2. Busy sleep: up_mdelay() / up_udelay()\nWeaknesses:\na. Does not actively trigger scheduling, occupy the CPU loading.\n\n3. New interfaces: Scheduled sleep: nxsched_sleep() / nxsched_usleep() / nxsched_msleep() / nxsched_ticksleep()\nStrengths:\na. Does not depend on the signal framework.\nb. Tick-based, without additional computational overhead.\n\nCurrently, the Nuttx driver framework extensively uses nxsig_* interfaces. However, the driver does not need to rely on signals or timespec conversion.\nTherefore, a new set of APIs is added to reduce dependencies on other modules.\n\n(This PR also aims to make signals optional, further reducing the code size of Nuttx.)\n\nSigned-off-by: chao an <anchao.archer@bytedance.com>",

    "sha": "761ee819568a52f1934ccf17bae20fe9816ebdec",
    "node_id": "C_kwDODZiUadoAKDc2MWVlODE5NTY4YTUyZjE5MzRjY2YxN2JhZTIwZmU5ODE2ZWJkZWM",
    "commit": {
      "author": {
        "name": "YAMAMOTO Takashi",
        "email": "yamamoto@midokura.com",
        "date": "2024-09-17T06:23:07Z"
      },
      "committer": {
        "name": "Xiang Xiao",
        "email": "xiaoxiang781216@gmail.com",
        "date": "2024-10-30T09:07:54Z"
      },
      "message": "move readv/writev to the kernel\n\ncurrently, nuttx implements readv/writev on the top of read/write.\nwhile it might work for the simplest cases, it's broken by design.\nfor example, it's impossible to make it work correctly for files\nwhich need to preserve data boundaries without allocating a single\ncontiguous buffer. (udp socket, some character devices, etc)\n\nthis change is a start of the migration to a better design.\nthat is, implement read/write on the top of readv/writev.\n\nto avoid a single huge change, following things will NOT be done in\nthis commit:\n\n* fix actual bugs caused by the original readv-based-on-read design.\n  (cf. https://github.com/apache/nuttx/pull/12674)\n\n* adapt filesystems/drivers to actually benefit from the new interface.\n  (except a few trivial examples)\n\n* eventually retire the old interface.\n\n* retire read/write syscalls. implement them in libc instead.\n\n* pread/pwrite/preadv/pwritev (except the introduction of struct uio,\n  which is a preparation to back these variations with the new\n  interface.)",

772: /****************************************************************************
773:  * Name: stmpe811_tscinitialize
774:  *
775:  * Description:
776:  *   Initialize the touchscreen controller.  This is really a part of the
777:  *   stmpe811_register logic,
778:  *
779:  ****************************************************************************/
780: 
781: static inline void stmpe811_tscinitialize(FAR struct stmpe811_dev_s *priv)
782: {
783:   uint8_t regval;
784: 
785:   iinfo("Initializing touchscreen controller\n");
786: 
787:   /* Enable TSC and ADC functions */
788: 
789:   regval = stmpe811_getreg8(priv, STMPE811_SYS_CTRL2);
790:   regval &= ~(SYS_CTRL2_TSC_OFF | SYS_CTRL2_ADC_OFF);
791:   stmpe811_putreg8(priv, STMPE811_SYS_CTRL2, regval);
792: 
793:   /* Enable the TSC global interrupts */
794: 
795:   regval  = stmpe811_getreg8(priv, STMPE811_INT_EN);
796:   regval |= (uint32_t)(INT_TOUCH_DET | INT_FIFO_TH | INT_FIFO_OFLOW);
797:   stmpe811_putreg8(priv, STMPE811_INT_EN, regval);
798: 
799:   /* Select Sample Time, bit number and ADC Reference */
800: 
801:   stmpe811_putreg8(priv, STMPE811_ADC_CTRL1, priv->config->ctrl1);
802: 
803:   /* Wait for 20 ms */
804: 
805:   up_mdelay(20);
806: 
807:   /* Select the ADC clock speed */
808: 
809:   stmpe811_putreg8(priv, STMPE811_ADC_CTRL2, priv->config->ctrl2);
810: 
811:   /* Select TSC pins in non-GPIO mode (AF=0) */
812: 
813:   regval  = stmpe811_getreg8(priv, STMPE811_GPIO_AF);
814:   regval &= ~(uint8_t)TSC_PIN_SET;
815:   stmpe811_putreg8(priv, STMPE811_GPIO_AF, regval);
816: 
817:   /* Select 2 nF filter capacitor */
818: 
819:   stmpe811_putreg8(priv, STMPE811_TSC_CFG, TSC_CFG_AVE_CTRL_4SAMPLES |
820:                    TSC_CFG_TOUCH_DELAY_500US | TSC_CFG_SETTLING_500US);
821: 
822:   /* Select single point reading */
823: 
824:   stmpe811_putreg8(priv, STMPE811_FIFO_TH, 1);
825: 
826:   /* Reset and clear the FIFO. */
827: 
828:   stmpe811_putreg8(priv, STMPE811_FIFO_STA, FIFO_STA_FIFO_RESET);
829:   stmpe811_putreg8(priv, STMPE811_FIFO_STA, 0);
830: 
831:   /* set the data format for Z value: 7 fractional part and 1 whole part */
832: 
833:   stmpe811_putreg8(priv, STMPE811_TSC_FRACTIONZ, 0x01);
834: 
835:   /* Set the driving capability of the device for TSC pins: 50mA */
836: 
837:   stmpe811_putreg8(priv, STMPE811_TSC_IDRIVE, TSC_IDRIVE_50MA);
838: 
839:   /* Enable the TSC.  Use no tracking index, touch-screen controller
840:    * operation mode (XYZ).
841:    */
842: 
843:   stmpe811_putreg8(priv, STMPE811_TSC_CTRL, TSC_CTRL_EN);
844: 
845:   /* Clear all the status pending bits */
846: 
847:   stmpe811_putreg8(priv, STMPE811_INT_STA, INT_ALL);
848: }

854: /****************************************************************************
855:  * Name: stmpe811_register
856:  *
857:  * Description:
858:  *  Enable TSC functionality.  GPIO4-7 must be available.  This function
859:  *  will register the touchscreen driver as /dev/inputN where N is the minor
860:  *  device number
861:  *
862:  * Input Parameters:
863:  *   handle    - The handle previously returned by stmpe811_register
864:  *   minor     - The input device minor number
865:  *
866:  * Returned Value:
867:  *   Zero is returned on success.  Otherwise, a negated errno value is
868:  *   returned to indicate the nature of the failure.
869:  *
870:  ****************************************************************************/
871: 
872: int stmpe811_register(STMPE811_HANDLE handle, int minor)
873: {
874:   FAR struct stmpe811_dev_s *priv = (FAR struct stmpe811_dev_s *)handle;
875:   char devname[DEV_NAMELEN];
876:   int ret;
877: 
878:   iinfo("handle=%p minor=%d\n", handle, minor);
879:   DEBUGASSERT(priv);
880: 
881:   /* Get exclusive access to the device structure */
882: 
883:   ret = nxmutex_lock(&priv->lock);
884:   if (ret < 0)
885:     {
886:       ierr("ERROR: nxsem_wait failed: %d\n", ret);
887:       return ret;
888:     }
889: 
890:   /* Make sure that the pins (4-7) need by the TSC are not already in use */
891: 
892:   if ((priv->inuse & TSC_PIN_SET) != 0)
893:     {
894:       ierr("ERROR: TSC pins is already in-use: %02x\n", priv->inuse);
895:       nxmutex_unlock(&priv->lock);
896:       return -EBUSY;
897:     }
898: 
899:   /* Initialize the TS structure fields to their default values */
900: 
901:   priv->minor     = minor;
902:   priv->penchange = false;
903:   priv->threshx   = 0;
904:   priv->threshy   = 0;
905: 
906:   /* Register the character driver */
907: 
908:   snprintf(devname, sizeof(devname), DEV_FORMAT, minor);
909:   ret = register_driver(devname, &g_stmpe811fops, 0666, priv);
910:   if (ret < 0)
911:     {
912:       ierr("ERROR: Failed to register driver %s: %d\n", devname, ret);
913:       nxmutex_unlock(&priv->lock);
914:       return ret;
915:     }
916: 
917:   /* Initialize the touchscreen controller */
918: 
919:   stmpe811_tscinitialize(priv);
920: 
921:   /* Inidicate that the touchscreen controller was successfully initialized */
922: 
923:   priv->inuse |= TSC_PIN_SET;                    /* Pins 4-7 are now in-use */
924:   priv->flags |= STMPE811_FLAGS_TSC_INITIALIZED; /* TSC function is initialized */
925:   nxmutex_unlock(&priv->lock);
926:   return ret;
927: }

929: /****************************************************************************
930:  * Name: stmpe811_tscworker
931:  *
932:  * Description:
933:  *   This function is called to handle a TSC interrupt.  It is not really
934:  *   an interrupt handle because it is called from the STMPE811 "bottom half"
935:  *   logic that runs on the worker thread.
936:  *
937:  ****************************************************************************/
938: 
939: void stmpe811_tscworker(FAR struct stmpe811_dev_s *priv, uint8_t intsta)
940: {
941:   uint16_t xdiff;    /* X difference used in thresholding */
942:   uint16_t ydiff;    /* Y difference used in thresholding */
943:   uint16_t x;        /* X position */
944:   uint16_t y;        /* Y position */
945:   bool     pendown;  /* true: pen is down */
946: 
947:   DEBUGASSERT(priv != NULL);
948: 
949:   /* Cancel the missing pen up timer */
950: 
951:   wd_cancel(&priv->wdog);
952: 
953:   /* Check for pen up or down from the TSC_STA bit in STMPE811_TSC_CTRL. */
954: 
955:   pendown = !!(stmpe811_getreg8(priv, STMPE811_TSC_CTRL) & TSC_CTRL_TSC_STA);
956: 
957:   /* Get exclusive access to the driver data structure */
958: 
959:   nxmutex_lock(&priv->lock);
960: 
961:   /* Handle the change from pen down to pen up */
962: 
963:   if (!pendown)
964:     {
965:       /* The pen is up.. reset thresholding variables.  FIFOs will read zero
966:        * if there is no data available (hence the choice of (0,0))
967:        */
968: 
969:       priv->threshx = 0;
970:       priv->threshy = 0;
971: 
972:       /* Ignore the interrupt if the pen was already up (CONTACT_NONE == pen
973:        * up and already reported; CONTACT_UP == pen up, but not reported)
974:        */
975: 
976:       if (priv->sample.contact == CONTACT_NONE ||
977:           priv->sample.contact == CONTACT_UP)
978:         {
979:           goto ignored;
980:         }
981: 
982:       /* A pen-down to up transition has been detected.  CONTACT_UP indicates
983:        * the initial loss of contact.  The state will be changed to
984:        * CONTACT_NONE after the loss of contact is sampled.
985:        */
986: 
987:        priv->sample.contact = CONTACT_UP;
988:     }
989: 
990:   /* The pen is down... check for data in the FIFO */
991: 
992:   else if ((intsta & (INT_FIFO_TH | INT_FIFO_OFLOW)) != 0)
993:     {
994:       /* Read the next x and y positions from the FIFO. */
995: 
996: #ifdef CONFIG_STMPE811_SWAPXY
997:       x = stmpe811_getreg16(priv, STMPE811_TSC_DATAX);
998:       y = stmpe811_getreg16(priv, STMPE811_TSC_DATAY);
999: #else
1000:       x = stmpe811_getreg16(priv, STMPE811_TSC_DATAY);
1001:       y = stmpe811_getreg16(priv, STMPE811_TSC_DATAX);
1002: #endif
1003: 
1004:       /* If we have not yet processed the last pen up event, then we
1005:        * cannot handle this pen down event. We will have to discard it.  That
1006:        * should be okay because there will be another FIFO event right behind
1007:        * this one.  Other kinds of data overruns are not harmful.
1008:        *
1009:        * Hmm.. a better design might be to disable FIFO interrupts when we
1010:        * detect pen up.  Then re-enable them when CONTACT_UP is reported.
1011:        * That would save processing interrupts just to discard the data.
1012:        */
1013: 
1014:       if (priv->sample.contact == CONTACT_UP)
1015:         {
1016:           /* We have not closed the loop on the last touch ... don't report
1017:            * anything.
1018:            */
1019: 
1020:           goto ignored;
1021:         }
1022: 
1023:       /* Perform a thresholding operation so that the results will be more
1024:        * stable. If the difference from the last sample is small, then ignore
1025:        * the event. REVISIT:  Should a large change in pressure also generate
1026:        * a event?
1027:        */
1028: 
1029:       xdiff = x > priv->threshx ? (x - priv->threshx) : (priv->threshx - x);
1030:       ydiff = y > priv->threshy ? (y - priv->threshy) : (priv->threshy - y);
1031: 
1032:       if (xdiff < CONFIG_STMPE811_THRESHX && ydiff < CONFIG_STMPE811_THRESHY)
1033:         {
1034:           /* Little or no change in either direction ...
1035:            * don't report anything.
1036:            */
1037: 
1038:           goto ignored;
1039:         }
1040: 
1041:       /* When we see a big difference, snap to the new x/y thresholds */
1042: 
1043:       priv->threshx       = x;
1044:       priv->threshy       = y;
1045: 
1046:       /* Update the x/y position in the sample data */
1047: 
1048:       priv->sample.x      = priv->threshx;
1049:       priv->sample.y      = priv->threshy;
1050: 
1051:       /* Update the Z pressure index */
1052: 
1053:       priv->sample.z      = stmpe811_getreg8(priv, STMPE811_TSC_DATAZ);
1054:       priv->sample.valid  = true;
1055: 
1056:       /* If this is the first (acknowledged) pen down report, then report
1057:        * this as the first contact.  If contact == CONTACT_DOWN, it will be
1058:        * set to set to CONTACT_MOVE after the contact is first sampled.
1059:        */
1060: 
1061:       if (priv->sample.contact != CONTACT_MOVE)
1062:         {
1063:           /* First contact */
1064: 
1065:           priv->sample.contact = CONTACT_DOWN;
1066:         }
1067:     }
1068: 
1069:   /* Pen down, but no data in FIFO */
1070: 
1071:   else
1072:     {
1073:       /* Ignore the interrupt... wait until there is data in the FIFO */
1074: 
1075:       goto ignored;
1076:     }
1077: 
1078:   /* We get here if (1) we just went from a pen down to a pen up state OR (2)
1079:    * We just get a measurement from the FIFO in a pen down state.  Indicate
1080:    * the availability of new sample data for this ID.
1081:    */
1082: 
1083:   priv->sample.id = priv->id;
1084:   priv->penchange = true;
1085: 
1086:   /* Notify any waiters that new STMPE811 data is available */
1087: 
1088:   stmpe811_notify(priv);
1089: 
1090:   /* If we think that the pen is still down, the start/re-start the pen up
1091:    * timer.
1092:    */
1093: 
1094: ignored:
1095:   nxmutex_unlock(&priv->lock);
1096:   if (priv->sample.contact == CONTACT_DOWN ||
1097:       priv->sample.contact == CONTACT_MOVE)
1098:     {
1099:       wd_start(&priv->wdog, STMPE811_PENUP_TICKS,
1100:                stmpe811_timeout, (wdparm_t)priv);
1101:     }
1102: 
1103:   /*  Reset and clear all data in the FIFO */
1104: 
1105:   stmpe811_putreg8(priv, STMPE811_FIFO_STA, FIFO_STA_FIFO_RESET);
1106:   stmpe811_putreg8(priv, STMPE811_FIFO_STA, 0);
1107: }
1108: 
1109: #endif /* CONFIG_INPUT && CONFIG_INPUT_STMPE811 && !CONFIG_STMPE811_TSC_DISABLE */

## 结论

本树中较一致的 touchscreen `read()` 语义是：

- 有事件：返回完整 `touch_sample_s`。
- 无事件且 `O_NONBLOCK`：返回 `-EAGAIN`。
- 无事件且阻塞模式：等待事件，而不是返回一个 `npoints == 0` 的成功读。
- `poll()` 只检测/通知可读状态；可读标志应在 `read()` 真正消费事件时清除，而不是在 poll setup 时清除。

当前 `gt9xx` 不完全符合：

- 无触摸时仍返回 `sizeof(struct touch_sample_s)`，其中 `npoints == 0`。
- 没有阻塞等待设施。
- 状态机实际上是“第一次读 DOWN，下一次读无条件 UP”，没有 MOVE。
- `int_pending` 的清理存在丢中断和重复 poll 风险。

## 对比

| 实现 | 无事件 read | 状态机 | poll/readiness 消费 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gt9xx` | 成功返回零点 sample | `DOWN -> 下一次read直接UP`，无 MOVE | 普通 I2C 分支无条件清 `int_pending`；UP 分支不清 |
| `ft5x06` | 非阻塞 `-EAGAIN`；阻塞等 `waitsem` | 硬件 DOWN/UP/CONTACT 映射为 DOWN/UP/MOVE | `valid` 在 sample 消费或丢弃时清；poll 不清 |
| `touchscreen_upper` | 非阻塞 `-EAGAIN`；阻塞等队列 | 状态由 lower-half 提供 | circbuf 被 read 消费；poll 仅检查队列 |
| `ads7843e`/`tsc2007`/`stmpe811` | 非阻塞 `-EAGAIN`；阻塞等信号量 | `NONE -> DOWN -> MOVE -> UP -> NONE` | `penchange` 在 sample 消费时清 |
| `mxt` | 同上 | 完整 NEW/MOVE/REPORT/LOST 状态机 | `event` 由 checksample test-and-clear |

## 建议的最小 `gt9xx_read()` 改法

最小、低风险修复应只解决非阻塞调用收到“成功的零点报告”：

1. 在 include 区增加：

```c
#include <fcntl.h>
```

2. 在重复点过滤后，不要无条件 `memcpy()`：

```c
if (sample.npoints == 0 &&
    (filep->f_oflags & O_NONBLOCK) != 0)
  {
    ret = -EAGAIN;
  }
else
  {
    memcpy(buffer, &sample, sizeof(sample));
  }
```

3. 建议额外保留真实 I2C 错误，避免把它覆盖成 `-EAGAIN`：

```c
ret = gt9xx_read_touch_data(priv, &sample);
if (ret < 0)
  {
    goto out_unlock;
  }
```

发生 I2C 错误时最好暂不清 `int_pending`，使下次 poll/read 可以重试。

这与 Apache NuttX 上游提交 `e884b6c3c8b2` 的 no-contact 修复方向一致；上游最小补丁明确保留了阻塞读的旧行为。增加 `ret < 0` 防护会比逐字回移上游补丁更稳妥，因为否则可能把 `-ETIMEDOUT` 等错误改写为 `-EAGAIN`。

不建议仅凭 `int_pending == false` 就直接返回 `-EAGAIN`：当前驱动仍允许主动读取硬件，且某些无可用 IRQ 的使用方式依赖这一点。

## 该最小修复没有解决的问题

### 1. 阻塞读仍不标准

`gt9xx` 没有 `waitsem`/`nwaiters`，因此只改 `gt9xx_read()` 无法正确实现阻塞。严格实现需要：

- ISR post 信号量；
- read 在检查事件与进入等待之间避免 lost wakeup；
- 初始化/销毁信号量；
- read 醒来后循环复查事件。

更长期可以把 GT9xx 改成 lower-half + `touch_register()`，直接复用 `touchscreen_upper` 的队列、阻塞和 poll 语义。

### 2. DOWN/MOVE/UP 状态机错误

当前流程：

- `gt9xx_read_touch_data()` 对任何正触点都标成 `TOUCH_DOWN`。
- 只要上次是 DOWN，下一次 `read()` 就直接生成 UP，甚至不要求有新 IRQ。
- MOVE 从不生成。
- 重复坐标仅转成 `npoints == 0`。

正确的一点状态机应为：

```text
NONE + data-ready/nonzero -> DOWN
ACTIVE + changed position -> MOVE
ACTIVE + data-ready/zero  -> UP
NONE + no contact         -> no event
```

需要同时区分：

- status bit 未 data-ready；
- data-ready 且触点数为零，即真实 release。

当前 helper 把两者都表现为 `npoints == 0`，所以不能只在 `gt9xx_read()` 中可靠修正。

### 3. `int_pending` 清理竞态

当前普通读取在 I2C 访问完成后才执行：

```c
priv->int_pending = false;
```

如果新 IRQ 在 I2C 期间把它设为 true，结尾的 false 会覆盖新事件。临界区只能保护赋值瞬间，不能保护整个“读取旧事件”的事务。

此外：

- I2C/状态清除失败仍会清 pending。
- synthetic UP 分支完全不清 pending，可能导致下一次 poll 立即再次可读，随后 read 得到零点或 `-EAGAIN`。
- poll waiter 数组由任务侧 mutex 修改，但 ISR 不使用同一个 IRQ-safe 锁，setup/teardown 与 ISR notify 有竞态。
- bool 只能合并多个 IRQ，无法区分读取期间到来的新事件。

完整修复宜使用工作队列加事件缓冲，或至少在处理开始时消费 pending、失败时恢复；但 synthetic UP 不读取/ACK 硬件，不能只简单提前清 flag。
